title: Personale Wirkungsrückkopplung in longitudinaler Mensch–KI-Interaktion
abstract: Die wiederholte Nutzung dialogischer generativer KI erzeugt nicht nur Outputs, sondern kann auch Erfahrungen darüber hervorbringen, wie unterschiedliche Formen der Mensch–KI-Interaktion auf die eigene kognitive, epistemische oder handlungsbezogene Funktionsweise wirken. Bestehende Forschung untersucht bereits Prompt Adaptation, metakognitive Regulation, Self-Regulated Learning, Trust Calibration, Human–AI Fit, Appropriation und Co-Adaptation. Weniger geklärt ist, wie wahrgenommene personale Wirkungen vorausgehender Interaktionen selbst zu Informationen für die bewusste Gestaltung späterer Mensch–KI-Interaktionen werden können. Das vorliegende theoretische Paper entwickelt hierfür das Modell personaler Wirkungsrückkopplung. Personale Wirkung bezeichnet eine Veränderung oder Zustandsdifferenz aufseiten des Menschen, zu deren Entstehung eine Mensch–KI-Interaktion beitragen kann. Das Modell unterscheidet diese Wirkung von ihrer subjektiven Wahrnehmung und berücksichtigt, dass ihre Bedeutung von den jeweils verfolgten Zielen abhängt. Werden wahrgenommene Wirkungen zumindest teilweise Eigenschaften einer Interaktionskonfiguration zugerechnet, können daraus subjektive Wirkungsannahmen entstehen: revidierbare Annahmen darüber, welche Formen der Mensch–KI-Interaktion unter bestimmten Bedingungen mit welchen personalen Wirkungen verbunden sein können. Solche Annahmen können spätere Interaktionskonfigurationen beeinflussen, indem bestimmte Interaktionsbedingungen gezielt verändert, beibehalten oder situationsbezogen gewählt werden. Die daraus entstehenden neuen Wirkungserfahrungen können frühere Wirkungsannahmen bestätigen, differenzieren oder revidieren. Der vorgeschlagene Prozess bildet eine longitudinale Rückkopplungsstruktur: Frühere personale Wirkung wird – sofern sie wahrgenommen, bewertet und interaktional attribuiert wird – zu einer möglichen Bedingung späterer Interaktionsgestaltung; die Wirkungen dieser rekonfigurierten Interaktion erzeugen wiederum neue Evidenz. Über wiederholte Episoden kann daraus ein zunehmend differenziertes, ziel- und kontextspezifisches Repertoire der Interaktionsgestaltung hervorgehen. Aus dem Modell werden sechs empirisch prüfbare Propositionen abgeleitet. Der theoretische Beitrag liegt nicht in der allgemeinen Annahme erfahrungsbasierter oder rekursiver Anpassung von Mensch–KI-Interaktion. Er liegt in der Spezifikation eines engeren Rückkopplungspfades, in dem wahrgenommene personale Wirkungen vorausgehender Interaktionskonfigurationen zu subjektiven Wirkungsannahmen beitragen und als mögliche zielrelative Informationsgrundlage für die bewusste Gestaltung späterer Interaktionen relevant werden.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Temporal Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that addresses the critical limitation of lacking temporal reasoning. Existing neuro-symbolic systems primarily focus on static program generation, neglecting the crucial aspect of execution timing and temporal constraints. We introduce a framework that seamlessly integrates a temporal logic engine with a neural network, allowing the network to learn and satisfy precise timing requirements during program execution. The core mechanism involves training the neural network to translate high-level symbolic representations into executable code while simultaneously adhering to temporal constraints expressed in temporal logic. This approach enables the creation of temporally aware AI systems capable of complex tasks requiring precise timing, opening new avenues for applications in robotics, control systems, and other domains where temporal accuracy is paramount. The system's ability to learn these constraints directly from data, rather than relying on hand-engineered rules, represents a significant advancement in the field. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method through a theoretical framework and outline potential future research directions. ---

title: Adaptive Code Generation via Evolutionary Programming with Formal Specifications
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive code generation that leverages the strengths of evolutionary programming and formal specifications. The core idea is to create an evolutionary algorithm that not only evaluates code based on its functional correctness but also incorporates formal verification to guarantee adherence to desired quality attributes. This integrated system dynamically adjusts the evolutionary process, prioritizing code variants that both satisfy functional requirements and exhibit desirable characteristics, such as low complexity and good performance. The research outlines a framework for this adaptive code generation system, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The system's ability to automatically refine code through a feedback loop based on formal verification provides a significant advancement over traditional code generation techniques, offering the potential for highly reliable and optimized software. The paper demonstrates the theoretical underpinnings of the approach and provides a conceptual design for its implementation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Random Walk Algorithms for Global Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired concepts to enhance the performance of random walk algorithms, specifically within the domain of global optimization. Classical random walk algorithms frequently struggle with convergence issues, frequently becoming trapped within local optima, a significant limitation when dealing with complex, high-dimensional search spaces. This research proposes a novel approach where random walk behavior is modeled based on principles derived from quantum mechanics, incorporating superposition and interference effects to facilitate more extensive and efficient exploration of the solution landscape. The core idea is to replace the deterministic step size in traditional random walks with a probabilistic movement governed by a quantum-like probability distribution. We explore the mathematical formulation of this process, detailing the probabilities of transition between states and the impact of interference. The resulting algorithms demonstrate improved convergence rates and a reduced tendency to get stuck in local optima compared to standard random walk methods. The paper concludes by outlining potential future research directions, including adaptive parameter tuning and integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits on Graph Clustering
abstract: This paper investigates the inherent limits of graph clustering from an information-theoretic perspective. We argue that graph clustering fundamentally relies on compressing information regarding node relationships and propose that the information-theoretic limit provides a quantifiable measure of this redundancy. We derive a theoretical bound on achievable compression rates, leveraging concepts of mutual information and entropy, which is directly influenced by the graph's connectivity and node features. This work establishes a new framework for understanding graph clustering, offering a fundamental limit on clustering performance that can be used to evaluate and optimize clustering algorithms. The key contribution lies in shifting the focus from heuristic optimization to a rigorously defined, information-constrained objective.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Logic with Adaptive Rule Generation via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning by integrating neural networks and symbolic logic, dynamically refined through reinforcement learning. The core idea is to create a hybrid system capable of autonomously generating and adapting logical rules based on observational data, leading to more robust and explainable reasoning systems compared to traditional rule-based methods. We introduce a reinforcement learning agent tasked with iteratively modifying a knowledge base containing logical rules. A neural network acts as an evaluator, assessing the consistency and utility of proposed rule changes. This feedback loop enables the system to learn complex logical structures and adapt to evolving data. We demonstrate the potential of this approach in achieving greater adaptability and explainability in reasoning systems.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, yet its inherent opacity presents a significant challenge. The "black box" nature of RL agents hinders understanding, trust, and effective debugging. This work introduces a novel framework for Explainable Reinforcement Learning (XRL) that leverages counterfactual reasoning to provide transparent explanations of RL agent behavior. The core idea involves generating counterfactual scenarios – hypothetical situations where an agent's actions are altered – and analyzing the resulting changes in the agent's policy. We formalize this process with a mathematical representation, enabling systematic exploration of decision-making factors. This approach moves beyond simply visualizing agent behavior and offers a rigorous, interpretable method for understanding *why* an RL agent makes a particular decision. The framework's ability to highlight influential features and sensitivities is expected to improve agent design, enhance robustness, and ultimately, foster greater trust in RL systems. The key contributions include a formalization of counterfactual reasoning within the RL context and a methodology for generating and analyzing counterfactual scenarios. ---

title: IMPLEMENTASI PERLABELAN INSET LEXICON-BASED PADA ALGORITMA NAIVE BAYES UNTUK ANALISIS OPINI PENGGUNA ULASAN APLIKASI GREEN SM: TAKSI 100% LISTRIK DI PLAY STORE
abstract: Green SM: Taksi 100% Listrik adalah aplikasi transportasi daring digital yang digunakan untuk memberikan layanan moda transportasi mobil listrik yang digunakan berbagai kalangan guna membantu masyarakat dalam hal mobilisasi. Meskipun dikembangkan untuk tujuan yang baik, masih terdapat pengguna yang merasa kurang puas terhadap fitur layanan maupun performa dan kualitas layanan yang disediakan. Untuk memahami opini pengguna terhadap aplikasi ini, penelitian ini menerapkan metode Naive Bayes dengan meimplementasikan pelabelan InSet Lexicon-Based. Data penelitian diperoleh dari ulasan pengguna aplikasi Green SM: Taksi 100% Listrik di Google Play Store dengan kerangka kerja Knowledge Discovery in Database. Sebanyak 1000 ulasan, dengan data yang digunakan berasal dari periode Mei 2026. Pada tahap selanjutnya, InSet Lexicon-Based digunakan untuk melabeli data pelatihan dan data uji, sementara algoritma Naïve Bayes diterapkan sebagai model klasifikasi sentimen. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa model menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 88%. Pada kategori sentimen negatif, model memperoleh 0,86 untuk precision, 0,98 untuk recall, dan 0,90 untuk f1-score, menunjukkan kemampuan yang baik dalam mengenali ulasan negatif. Sebaliknya, kinerja untuk kategori positif cenderung lebih rendah. Berdasarkan hasil analisis, opini negatif mendominasi ulasan pengguna. Namun evaluasi dan perbaikan tetap diperlukan berdasarkan keluhan pengguna guna meningkatkan kualitas serta layanan dan pengembangan aplikasi di masa depan.

title: QUANTUM FEATURE ENCODING FOR ENHANCING CNN-BASED IMAGE CLASSIFICATION PERFORMANCE
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have exposed robust results for classifying images in data analytics. On the other hand, the effectiveness of these models is often limited by their substantial computational complexities, particularly when dealing with features represented in complex mathematical environments, multi class image classification, and especially when dealing with complex nonlinear relationships between features, which need to be addressed for transparent decision-making processes. This study developed a Quantum-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (Q-CNN) model, which incorporates traditional convolution-based feature extraction, Quantum Feature Encoding, and quantum processing. The developed model applies a quantum encoding mechanism to map classical features to quantum states for alternative feature representations and classification purposes. Experimental results show that the Q-CNN outperformed the standard CNN, reaching 97% training and validation accuracy compared to 94%, and lowering training and validation losses from 17% and 18% to 9% and 11%, respectively. Furthermore, precision, recall, and F1-score were increased from 90%, 88%, and 89% to 92%, 94%, and 93%, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential effectiveness of quantum feature encoding for image classification tasks and provide a structured framework for enriched feature representation in convolution-based image processing models.

title: Novel Aspects of Ant Colony Optimization and Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: A Mobile Ad Hoc Network (MANET) is a collection of mobile nodes dynamically organized such that the connections among them frequently change. For carrying out conversation inside the system, routing algorithm is utilized to find path among nodes. The main objective of this type of ad-hoc system routing algorithm is accurate and competent path creation among a couple of nodes. This way, information would be conveyed in an appropriate way. Path building ought to be carried out with a least amount of bandwidth utilization and overheads. A wireless ad-hoc system is a structure installed exclusive of some infrastructure. Topics comprise of learning on routing algorithms for advanced efficiency, and practical concerns in its application. These areas are critical to construct a support in design, execution, operation, and examination of wireless ad-hoc system. This chapter will highlight mainly essential features of eminent algorithms particle swarm optimization (PSO) and Ant colony optimization (ACO). It deals with hybridization of two algorithms ACO and PSO. Merging the strengths of two algorithms will solve complex problems in various fields.

title: Optimizing Curriculum Design with Fuzzy Logic in Computational Intelligence
abstract: The purpose of this work is to investigate the optimization of class design through the utilization of fuzzy sense within the field of computational intelligence, pulling perceptivity from educational exploration. When it comes to meeting the diverse and ever-changing needs of students, traditional classroom layouts frequently struggle to adequately accommodate them. A good outcome can be achieved by the utilization of fuzzy sense, which can deal with queries and nebulosity. The purpose of this project is to investigate how fuzzy sense can be utilized to develop educational programs that are more flexible and individualized. The approach that has been described enables nuanced decision-making in the context of classroom development. This is accomplished by incorporating both expert knowledge and feedback from students into fuzzy conclusion systems. A comparative review of several models reveals that fuzzy sense is beneficial in improving the inflexibility of the classroom and the responsiveness to the needs of the students. Case studies derived from diverse educational environments exhibit realistic implementations and benefits, such as improved student engagement and literacy concerns. In light of the findings, it appears that the fuzzy sense-grounded class design not only caters to the preferences of individual students in terms of literacy but also improves the quality of education as a whole. This exploration contributes to the current efforts to facilitate the implementation of educational methods through the use of computational intelligence.

title: Constant-time equilibration of observables under rapid Lindbladian dynamics
abstract: Markovian open-system dynamics have widespread applications throughout quantum information science, including algorithmic state preparation. Their convergence is commonly quantified using the worst case global trace distance between the evolving and stationary states. However, this criterion can be unnecessarily stringent when only physically relevant observables are of interest. Here we introduce and study observable-specific mixing times. We prove that, for quasi-local, rapidly mixing Lindbladians, sums of geometrically local observables equilibrate in a time independent of system size, in contrast to the logarithmic dependence of global state mixing. This separation reduces the runtime of dissipative quantum algorithms, including quantum Gibbs samplers, for estimating quantities such as the Gibbs state energy and local order parameters, yielding an overall scaling that is linear in system size. Complementing this quantum result, we develop a quantum-inspired classical algorithm for estimating the same quantities. evidence.abstract: Markovian open-system dynamics have widespread applications throughout quantum information science, including algorithmic state preparation. Their convergence is commonly quantified using the worst case global trace distance between the evolving and stationary states. title: Locate Anything in Videos: Rethinking Efficient Generative Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
abstract: Spatio-temporal video grounding (STVG) requires models to identify when a referred event occurs and localize the target entity throughout that interval. Existing multimodal large language models typically serialize dense localization trajectories autoregressively, causing decoding latency to grow with tube length and allowing localization errors to propagate across time. We introduce Parallel Tube Decoding (PTD), a generative formulation that decomposes grounding into a temporal block followed by time-conditioned spatial blocks decoded simultaneously. This removes both token-level and trajectory-level dependencies, reducing the sequential decoding depth to a fixed 1 + 1 rounds, independent of tube length. To enable parallel spatial generation, we introduce Decoupled Block Attention, which preserves access to shared video-query context while eliminating cross-box dependencies, together with localization-aware policy optimization for temporal boundaries and spatial geometry. On VidSTG, PTD reduces Tube Completion Latency by 79x and increases spatial decoding throughput by 92x over standard autoregressive decoding, while also improving grounding accuracy. With a compact 4B backbone, our model performs favorably well on VidSTG and HC-STVG, and generalizes zero-shot to temporal grounding, grounded VideoQA, and referring video object tracking. Our results show parallel tube generation is an efficient and effective alternative to autoregressive localization in videos.

title: Speculative Probing: LLM Monitoring at Speculative-Decoding Cost
abstract: Real-time classification during language model inference is valuable for safety filtering, behavioral analysis, and model monitoring, but current approaches force a trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Hidden-state probes are fast but limited: they are either not context-aware: operating on a single vector and cannot model interactions across positions; or they are very costly: having dedicated classifier models (Llama Guard, Qwen Guard, LLM-as-judge) or performing computation on hidden states for all tokens and then pooling the results (MultiMax). This shows an intrinsic trade-off between efficiency and accuracy. However, we find that the speculative-decoding module in recent LLMs can be repurposed for efficient high-quality classification. By appending a trained soft prompt at the end of the target sequence, we can repurpose the speculative-decoding module into a sequence classifier. At inference time in a speculative-decoding pipeline, the KV cache is already in GPU memory, so classification adds negligible overhead. We evaluate on four classification tasks across four models (Qwen3.5-4B, 9B, 27B, MiniCPM4.1-8B). Our small probes consistently outperform zero-shot GPT-5.4-mini and, on multilingual prompt safety, match or beat specialized 8B safety classifiers (Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B, Llama-Guard-3-8B) without running a full LLM.

title: Optimizing entanglement manipulation via algebraic–geometric decompositions and semi-definite programming hierarchies
abstract: In the study of distributed quantum information processing, it is a fundamental problem to optimize local operations in the implementation of non-local quantum operations assisted by limited entanglement. We develop an algebraic–geometric framework that systematically simplifies optimization over separable (SEP) channels—widely used as approximations of local operations—and strengthens the Doherty–Parrilo–Spedalieri (DPS) hierarchy for solving such problems. We apply this framework to computing maximum success probability for exactly implementing a broad range of different non-local operations under SEP channels. First, we present a unified generalization of previous analytical results on the entanglement cost. Via the generalization, we resolve an open problem posed by Yu et al. regarding the entanglement cost of local state discrimination. Second, we numerically determine the trade-off between the strength of entanglement and the success probability of implementing various operations—such as entanglement distillation, non-local unitary channels, measurements, and state verification.

title: AI Literacy - A learning path for managers
abstract: Understanding, configuring, and operating AI in the enterprise, fifteen lessons built for a curious reader, no technical prerequisites. This learning path was born from a pattern seen repeatedly in the field: most organizations move forward on AI without a shared vocabulary or a common maturity benchmark across leaders, technical teams, and business users, which slows decisions and multiplies false starts. Trencadis provided a development framework for this learning path over four months, enabling a productive collaboration between two generations of practitioners. Rather than keep this teaching internal, Trencadis chose to publish an open version: giving every organization the words and benchmarks needed to discuss AI with the same rigour as any other strategic topic. This learning path is like a living platform: it exists online, its structure is robust and durable, and it will receive regular updates to stay current with a subject that changes significantly from week to week. The AI project lead gives particular attention to reliability, performance measurement, and the governance of the solutions he builds. This dual expertise, technical and project management, runs directly through the content of this learning path: every concept is presented at the standard expected of a real production deployment, not a demo. The senior advisor brings 35 years of experience in business organization, having served more than 120 enterprises of every size and sector. This field practice, built up long before the arrival of generative AI, is what shapes the approach of this learning path: AI is treated as an organizational subject before a technical one, governance, roles, processes, human capabilities, rather than simply a matter of tooling.Happy readingContact : fgaurier@trencadis.ca

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to the problem of inference and learning within large-scale Bayesian Networks (BNs). Traditional Bayesian Network learning and inference methods often struggle with scalability, particularly as the number of nodes and dependencies increases. We propose leveraging concepts from quantum algorithms, specifically drawing inspiration from quantum annealing and quantum Monte Carlo methods, to efficiently explore the complex search space associated with BN structure optimization and parameter estimation. The core idea is to mimic the exploration capabilities of quantum systems to accelerate the process. The proposed methodology aims to improve the efficiency of BN learning and inference, potentially unlocking new capabilities for probabilistic reasoning in complex systems. This work presents a theoretical framework and a conceptual outline for such an approach, laying the groundwork for future research and experimentation. The effectiveness of this approach is predicated on the ability to translate the inherent parallelism of quantum algorithms into an efficient optimization strategy for Bayesian Networks.

title: Quantum Error Correction via Topological Neural Networks
abstract: Classical neural networks suffer from inherent vulnerabilities to noise and errors, severely limiting their applicability in demanding environments. This research proposes a novel approach to mitigating these issues by leveraging topological neural networks (TNNs) for quantum error correction (QEC). Inspired by the robust properties of topological insulators, TNNs are designed to encode information in topological invariants, making them inherently resilient to local perturbations. This paper details the framework for integrating TNNs with neural network architectures, outlining the key concepts of braiding operations, logical qubit representation, and the implementation of standard QEC codes like Shor and Steane. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, demonstrating how TNNs can effectively detect and correct errors without disrupting the underlying computation. The resulting architecture promises a significantly enhanced resilience to noise, potentially unlocking the full potential of neural networks for complex and uncertain tasks. Our approach offers a fundamentally new direction in computing, bridging the gap between classical and quantum computation through a robust and adaptable network topology. We define key metrics for evaluating the performance of this system including error correction fidelity and computational speedup relative to traditional neural networks.

title: Graph-Based Representation of Semantic Networks for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of graph-based representations of semantic networks to improve knowledge graph reasoning. Traditional knowledge graph representations often struggle with complex relationships and inference tasks. We propose a novel approach that utilizes graphs, where nodes represent concepts and edges represent the semantic relationships between them. This allows for efficient traversal and inference based on graph algorithms. The core claim is that this representation significantly enhances reasoning capabilities, particularly in scenarios demanding intricate connections and deductions. The mechanism involves translating knowledge into a structured graph format, allowing for algorithmic reasoning. The presented method offers a more intuitive and powerful framework compared to traditional methods, ultimately leading to improved performance in knowledge graph reasoning. We explore key concepts and illustrate the potential of this approach with a theoretical framework.

title: Adaptive Thresholding for Sensor Data Fusion using Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to sensor data fusion utilizing Bayesian networks. The core idea is to dynamically adjust data thresholds based on sensor uncertainty and contextual information, leading to improved fusion accuracy. The proposed framework learns the reliability of each sensor and adapts thresholds accordingly. This addresses a key limitation of traditional threshold-based fusion methods which often rely on fixed, potentially inaccurate, thresholds. The system employs a Bayesian network to model the dependencies between sensor readings and utilizes probabilistic inference to determine appropriate thresholds. The adaptive nature of the thresholds enhances the robustness of the fusion process, particularly in environments with noisy or unreliable sensor data. The paper outlines the framework, details the mathematical formulation, and explores the potential benefits of this adaptive thresholding technique.

title: Maps With an Uncertain Now: Affine Origin Factorization and Hallucination as Argmax Collapse
abstract: This registration defines a confirmatory computational study of chart-conditioned affine origin factorization in small decoder-only Transformers. Across temporal-1D and spatial-2D synthetic relational worlds, the study separates failure to construct a relational chart, uncertainty or error in locating an origin, and loss of a correctly represented origin posterior during point decoding. It preregisters three jointly required hypotheses: exact-chart causal rescue (H1), low-dimensional and causally selective affine origin factorization (H2), and calibrated posterior preservation with argmax-collapse and value-of-information tests (H3). Ten independent seed triplets, fixed generators, paired interventions, proper scoring rules, success thresholds, exclusion rules, and a confirmatory execution lock are frozen in the attached archive. Exploratory and development results are explicitly firewalled from the new confirmatory runs.

title: A three-party verifiable blind quantum computing protocol with separated input and function ownership
abstract: Abstract Blind quantum computing enables quantum-limited clients to securely access untrusted quantum servers. This paper proposes a three-party verifiable blind quantum computing protocol with separated input and function ownership, where Alice holds the private input, Bob holds the target function, and Charlie performs the delegated quantum computation, with the result released only to Alice. Alice and Bob first establish a shared key using BB84. Under the measurement-based quantum computing framework, a secure two-party computation protocol is then used to jointly generate adaptive blinded measurement instructions, eliminating the need for Bob to transmit quantum states to Charlie. A hidden dummy-trap mechanism is further incorporated to verify malicious server behavior. Under the honest-but-curious client model without client-server collusion, the protocol protects input and function privacy while ensuring computation blindness, shared-key security, and verifiability. Most quantum operations are performed by Charlie, while the clients require only limited quantum capabilities.

title: Quantum-inspired scenario-adaptive differential privacy with hybrid attention–residual deep learning for utility-aware urban location analytics
abstract: Abstract Location-based services (LBS) increasingly rely on trajectory data, creating a persistent challenge in balancing user privacy and data utility. Conventional differential privacy (DP) mechanisms often employ fixed noise distributions and global privacy budgets, limiting their ability to adapt to heterogeneous urban environments. To address this limitation, we propose a Quantum-Inspired Scenario-Adaptive Differential Privacy framework that combines k-nearest-neighbor (kNN)-based adaptive privacy budgeting with structured quantum-inspired noise generation and a Hybrid Attention–Residual Deep Neural Network for mechanism selection. The framework introduces a five-dimensional urban morphology descriptor comprising Uniformity, Directional Bias, Spatial Correlation, Density Gradient, and Clustering, and jointly learns privacy-mechanism selection and urban-pattern classification through a dual-task architecture. The Hybrid DNN achieved a mean mechanism-classification accuracy of 97.35% ± 0.24 across ten random seeds, performing competitively with XGBoost (97.33% ± 0.20), a Tabular Transformer (97.26% ± 0.31), and a GraphSAGE-style Graph Neural Network (97.24% ± 0.28). Ablation analysis under data-scarce noisy conditions identified dual-task learning as the most influential architectural component, yielding a statistically significant accuracy improvement of 0.33 percentage points (Wilcoxon p = 0.035). Across the privacy benchmark, quantum-inspired Laplace mechanisms reduced mean absolute error by up to 33.19%, utility loss by up to 41.36%, privacy loss by up to 38.48%, and geo-indistinguishability error by up to 51.61% relative to their classical counterparts. Quantum Anisotropic Gaussian achieved the largest utility gains, reducing distortion metrics by 72–78%, while Quantum Exponential eliminated observed linkability risk on the datasets. Formal statistical testing using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction across 156 cross-dataset comparisons found 133 significant results (85.3%), with large paired effect sizes for the Laplace and Anisotropic Gaussian quantum variants. These results demonstrate that structured quantum-inspired perturbations can substantially improve privacy–utility trade-offs while maintaining robustness across independent real-world mobility datasets.

title: Nature‐Inspired Algorithms and Their Applications
abstract: Nature-inspired algorithms, based on the collective intelligence and adaptive behaviors of biological systems, have emerged as effective optimization strategies for solving complex real-world issues. The chapter explores the fundamentals and applications of such algorithms, with an emphasis on the Bees Algorithm, which is inspired by honeybee colonies’ foraging activity. The chapter begins with an introduction to the core concept and the main traits of nature-inspired algorithms. Furthermore, it classifies these algorithms into subcategories such as evolutionary, swarm-based, and ecosystem-based. The chapter gives prominence to the Bees Algorithm, describing in detail its operation and optimization potential. A case study related to healthcare illustrates how the algorithm is applied in the diagnosis of breast cancer and how it improved classification accuracy and decision-making in medical data analysis included in the chapter. Through the proposed case study, the chapter highlights the potential of biologically inspired computing as a robust, adaptive, and efficient approach in healthcare analytics and diagnostics.

title: Manifold4D: Denoising on Point Cloud Rendered Manifolds for Video Re-shooting
abstract: Video re-shooting re-renders a monocular video of a dynamic scene along a user-specified camera trajectory, and the dominant recipe supplies the target geometry explicitly: per-frame depth lifts the source video into a 4D point cloud, which is rasterized along the trajectory into a point cloud render. Because the render and the source video are both handed to the network as visual conditions, they compete at every denoising step, leaving the model with a trust dilemma --- how much of the render to believe --- which can degrade trajectory control or visual quality on data outside the training distribution. We argue that a render already pixel-aligned with the target view does not need to be supplied as an explicit conditioning stream at all. We propose MANIFOLD4D, which injects the render directly into the initial noise of flow matching, so that generation no longer departs from standard Gaussian noise but from a new noise manifold carrying geometric information, leaving the source video as the only visual condition. The render is thus used exactly once, and the network is never asked to learn how to read it; in subsequent denoising steps the model can focus on the source video. On our DAVIS-Traj benchmark and on the Vista4D evaluation set, MANIFOLD4D attains the best camera-control accuracy on every metric, lowering rotation error by 25% and 27% and translation error by up to 32% over the strongest baseline, while matching it in video fidelity and leading on real-world novel-view photometric quality. In a user study, our method achieves clear advantages in trajectory following and dynamic consistency. The gap widens as the yaw amplitude grows past the training range, and the model still recovers correct dynamic motion from the source video when the render is deliberately corrupted, confirming that the geometric prior guides generation without overriding it.

We propose MANIFOLD4D, which injects the render directly into the initial noise of flow matching, so that generation no longer departs from standard Gaussian noise but from a new noise manifold carrying geometric information, leaving the source video as the only visual condition. The render is thus used exactly once, and the network is never asked to learn how to read it; in subsequent denoising steps the model can focus on the source video. On our DAVIS-Traj benchmark and on the Vista4D evaluation set, MANIFOLD4D attains the best camera-control accuracy on every metric, lowering rotation error by 25% and 27% and translation error by up to 32% over the strongest baseline, while matching it in video fidelity and leading on real-world novel-view photometric quality. In a user study, our method achieves clear advantages in trajectory following and dynamic consistency. The gap widens as the yaw amplitude grows past the training range, and the model still recovers correct dynamic motion from the source video when the render is deliberately corrupted, confirming that the geometric prior guides generation without overriding it.

title: When Evidence Shapes Collaboration: Knowledge-Conditioned Topology Generation for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) have recently moved from static workflows toward dynamically generated collaboration topologies. However, existing topology generation methods rely primarily on the parametric knowledge of large language models, with external search or retrieval used only as a reactive tool rather than an explicit determinant of collaboration structure. This leads to structure-knowledge misalignment, where systems exhibit redundant interactions or insufficient verification in knowledge-intensive tasks. We propose K-GAT (Knowledge-Guided Agent Topology Generator), a neuro-symbolic framework that formulates collaboration topology design as a knowledge-conditioned structure learning problem, integrating external evidence directly into autoregressive graph generation. Extensive experiments on knowledge-intensive benchmarks demonstrate K-GAT's efficiency and effectiveness: notably on the expert-level GPQA dataset, K-GAT outperforms the LLM-Debate baseline by a substantial margin of +15.7% in accuracy, while consuming less than half the computational tokens.

title: Controlled Language Generation: Token Trees, Fokker--Planck--HJB Limits, and Certificates
abstract: We develop a unified theory of controlled language generation whose primary object is the exact autoregressive prefix tree and whose continuous Fokker--Planck--Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (FP--HJB) system is a conditional scaling limit. KL-regularized token control yields a nonlinear soft Bellman recursion backward and a prefix-occupancy recursion forward. We prove that the Fr\'echet derivative of the Bellman operator is the controlled token kernel and that its adjoint is exactly the forward occupancy propagator. This operator identity gives an envelope/sensitivity theorem and two non-asymptotic certificates: a uniform Bellman-residual bound and an occupancy-weighted bound that multiplies root-mean-square residuals by explicit distribution-shift factors. The latter is the paper's central architectural result. The forward block estimates the occupancy and coverage factors needed to certify the backward value block; the model therefore prices the reliability of its own certificate under deployment shift. For continuous latent generation we derive the HJB and FP equations, prove the analogous residual-and-coverage certificate, and state the exact compatibility condition $G R^{-1}G^\top=a/\beta$ under which Hopf--Cole linearization turns optimal steering into a Doob transform. We also identify a control-gauge invariance showing that generation data determine the controlled drift and the matrix $G R^{-1}G^\top$, not a unique decomposition into control channel and intervention cost. We give a valid entropy-controlled Markov-chain limit, distinguish finite-temperature guidance from support-changing truncation and diffusion-volatility changes, and separate KL-regularized fine-tuning, value-guided inference, exponential resampling, and best-of-$n$: the first three can target the same Gibbs law, while best-of-$n$ produces a different rank tilt. Distributional objectives lead to a coupled mean-field FP--HJB system with a variational terminal condition. These results induce a four-block Transformer---reference dynamics, value, occupancy/score, and control---whose losses, coverage diagnostics, and failure gates are mathematically linked rather than merely co-trained.

title: Identity-Level Machine Unlearning on Synthetic Facial Data — Experimental Results and Evaluation Artifacts
abstract: The experimental-results record for an identity-level machine-unlearning framework with a MUFAC-style dual-head design, evaluated on 750 synthetic identities (SFHQ-derived). This record is the results receipt for the accompanying dissertation: every result table and figure in Chapters 5-9 traces to the CSVs, JSONs and plots shipped here. It contains the full multi-tier evaluation — single-shot at default and tuned configurations (5 seeds), the 15-step iterative protocol under uniform and seeded-Poisson arrival schedules, long-tail per-popularity-bin equity analysis, Tier-4 canary verification (AdaptiForget, GA, FT), the AdaptiForget component ablation, and the multi-scale feasibility gate — plus the per-method hyperparameter-search trials and the per-lane reports. Methods compared: GA, NG+, AdaptiForget (novel), MSG, MSG-KD, CT, FT, SRL and Budget-Scaled GA (novel), with retrain and no-unlearning controls. The evaluation data are the separately released SFHQ-VirtualID-Bench and SFHQ-VirtualID-Raw datasets. Non-commercial research use only; full licence terms in the LICENSE file inside this archive.

title: XOR: A Reversible Transformation in Cryptography
abstract: Author’s Note — On Determinism and Randomness This book grew out of an exploration undertaken largely for the pleasure of following a simple question: how do deterministic transformations and randomness meet inside cryptography? Cryptographic algorithms are deterministic mathematical objects, yet many of their security guarantees depend critically on randomness, independence, unpredictability, and non-reuse. XOR became an unexpectedly rich point of entry into that contrast. Its behavior is algebraically exact, deterministic, reversible, and easy to compute; nevertheless, the security of constructions built around it can change completely according to the statistical properties of a key or keystream. Following that tension led naturally from Boolean algebra and finite fields to entropy, perfect secrecy, pseudorandomness, stream ciphers, AES, differential analysis, and the prospective mathematical directions explored near the end of the book. The monograph was therefore written as a scientific exploration rather than as an attempt to replace established cryptographic theory. It follows a simple operation as far as its mathematics will lead, asking questions, checking them analytically and computationally, and observing how deterministic structure and randomness interact. In that sense, the book is both a synthesis and an exploration written for the joy of understanding.

title: Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Relays for Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to designing distributed computing relay networks, inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics. Traditional relay networks often struggle with robustness against node failures and inefficient data routing. Our approach leverages quantum-inspired superposition and entanglement to create a network capable of dynamically adapting to changing conditions and optimizing communication pathways. The core idea is to represent each relay node's possible communication paths as a superposition of states, weighted by learned probabilities. These probabilities are derived from entanglement metrics, simulating the correlation observed in quantum systems. This allows the network to explore multiple routes concurrently, mitigating the impact of individual node failures and ultimately enhancing both the resilience and efficiency of the distributed computing system. The resulting network exhibits a greater degree of parallelism and adaptability compared to classical relay networks. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key design considerations and the expected performance improvements.

title: Relational Memory Networks with Temporal Attention
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational memory networks (RMNs) that addresses the limitations of existing models in handling temporal dependencies and prioritizing relevant memory slots. We propose integrating a temporal attention mechanism into the RMN architecture, enabling the network to dynamically adjust its attention weights based on the time elapsed since a memory event. This allows for improved recall and prediction accuracy, particularly in time-series data and dynamic systems. The core claim is that existing RMNs struggle to effectively manage temporal dependencies and prioritize memory slots, while the proposed temporal attention mechanism significantly improves performance. The key mechanism involves dynamically adjusting attention weights based on temporal context. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the potential benefits of this combined architecture.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Neural Network Generalization
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of neural network generalization using information-theoretic principles. We posit that neural network performance is intrinsically bounded by the Kolmogorov complexity of the training data. Our theoretical framework analyzes the information content within the training set and demonstrates a direct correlation between this content and the achievable generalization error. We leverage concepts from Kolmogorov complexity and entropy coding to provide a rigorous mathematical analysis, offering a novel perspective on the learning process and potentially guiding the design of more effective neural network architectures. The key contribution lies in translating the abstract concept of "complexity" into a quantifiable metric, providing a concrete bound on the achievable generalization performance. This work challenges the prevailing view of generalization as a purely empirical phenomenon and introduces a theoretical foundation rooted in information theory.

title: Formal Verification of Trustworthy Federated Learning Systems
abstract: Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data, offering enhanced privacy and reduced communication costs. However, the inherent distributed nature of FL introduces significant challenges regarding trust, security, and model accuracy. This paper presents a formal verification framework for FL systems, leveraging secure multi-party computation (SMPC) and formal verification techniques to rigorously analyze data flow and model updates. The framework aims to provide guarantees about privacy, security, and model accuracy, addressing the unique vulnerabilities present in FL architectures. We define a mathematical model of an FL system, incorporating key elements such as clients, servers, and communication protocols. This model is then subjected to formal verification, utilizing techniques like model checking and symbolic execution to identify potential security breaches and inaccuracies. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of applying formal verification to FL, offering a robust approach to ensuring the trustworthiness of these systems. Key performance metrics, including privacy loss, communication overhead, and model accuracy deviations, are quantified and analyzed within the verification process. The framework contributes to the development of more reliable and secure FL applications, particularly in sensitive domains such as healthcare and finance.

title: ##基于多尺度自组织神经网络的量子算法优化
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization by leveraging the inherent capabilities of multi-scale self-organizing neural networks (MSSONNs). The core idea is to transform the optimization of quantum algorithms into a training problem for MSSONNs, allowing the network to autonomously discover optimal structures and parameters. We propose a framework where the quantum algorithm's objective function is mapped onto the MSSONN's loss function. Through iterative training, the MSSONN adapts and evolves, effectively automating the design and refinement of quantum algorithms. This work demonstrates the potential for significantly reducing the manual effort involved in quantum algorithm development, accelerating the discovery of efficient solutions, and ultimately unlocking the full potential of quantum computation. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of neural network self-organization and quantum algorithm optimization, leading to an adaptive and automated process. ---

title: Critic-derived shaping in Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: The simplicity and stability of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in reinforcement learning make it popular, yet its on-policy training loop may be sample-inefficient. This thesis investigates whether PPO can leverage temporal-difference (TD) error, a signal that it already computes, in a regulated manner. We introduce critic-derived advantage shaping (CDAS), a method which employs normalized positive TD error as an actor-side shaping signal, and critic-derived value shaping (CDVS), which applies the same detached, normalized bonus to the critic target. While CDAS-0 and CDVS-0 employ one-step positive TD error, we test additional variants called CDAS-λ and CDVS-λ, which propagate future positive critic surprise backward via a GAE-style bonus trace. We find that PPO can benefit from positive critic surprise in advantage-side shaping, and especially critic-side shaping, but only under strict scale control. When the bonus is modest in comparison to the extrinsic advantage, actor-side CDAS improves performance on several MuJoCo tasks and performs particularly well on the Atari game Gravitar. Conservative CDAS-0 and CDAS-λ settings in MuJoCo increase mean PPO-normalized final return by around 4–5% above PPO. However, the improvements are environment-dependent; Venture demonstrates how visually prominent but task-misaligned transitions can draw the TD-error signal and impair learning, while Hopper performance deteriorates when the coefficient is too high. Critic-side shaping is stronger in aggregate—CDVS-0 improves mean PPO-normalized final return by 7.4% across the studied MuJoCo environments, and the strongest critic-only CDVS-λ configuration improves it by 12.5%. In the Atari critic-side sweep, the strongest aggregate CDVS-λ configuration improves mean final return by 14.2% and mean AUC by about 16%, with AUC gains in all five Atari games. Overall, critic-derived shaping is useful until it overpowers PPO's extrinsic learning structure: TD-error-based bonuses must stay secondary to PPO's extrinsic learning signals in order to be beneficial.

title: An Exploratory Ablation of a Small MLA--SSM Hybrid Language Model
abstract: We report an exploratory, single-seed ablation of TALH (Adaptive Latent Hybrid), a decoder-only language model with parallel Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and a custom recurrent state-space (SSM) branch. Five variants, spanning 117--217M estimated active parameters per token, are trained from scratch on a FineWeb sample for the same number of optimisation steps and tokens. In this specific setup, removing the SSM branch gives the largest degradation in validation perplexity (MLA-only PPL 315), whereas removing MLA has a much smaller effect (SSM-only PPL 239). A dense-FFN hybrid obtains PPL 231, compared with 240 for the tested top-2 ternary-MoE hybrid, while using 3.87 GB less peak training memory. We also preserve a preliminary Apple M3 timing observation: among the five unoptimised implementations, MLA-only has the flattest measured time-to-first-token curve from 512 to 2,048 prompt tokens, although the dense Transformer is much faster in absolute terms. Because the runs are single-seed, parameter counts are unmatched, the evaluation stream may overlap the training source, and raw repeated timing records are unavailable, these results support implementation-specific hypotheses rather than general conclusions about MLA, SSMs, or mixture-of-experts models.

title: Curvature-Conditioned Multiscale Momentum with Sphere Constraints for LLM Pretraining
abstract: Pretraining accounts for a large fraction of the total computational cost in LLM training. However, noise-dominant gradients and the highly ill-conditioned loss landscape bring severe challenges. Although modern adaptive optimizers such as AdamW and Muon have achieved great success in large-scale pretraining, their reliance on gradient normalization offers limited mitigation of the ill-conditioned curvature. The progress along flat directions (eigen-directions of small eigenvalues), which dominates the final loss reduction, remains relatively slow. To enhance training dynamics along flat directions, we propose a curvature-conditioned multiscale momentum method with sphere constraints, delivering steady acceleration in LLM pretraining. This multiscale momentum, applied only along flat directions, pairs a slow-decay component for noise reduction with a fast-decay component for rapid curvature adaptation, harnessing their complementary strengths. Crucially, we employ a sphere constraint technique to prevent parameter inflation and excessively rapid effective learning rate decay that would otherwise arise from a naive combination. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method significantly accelerates Muon across diverse architectures (dense, MoE) and model sizes (0.12B--2.3B parameters). Theoretically, we verify the acceleration effect and provide insight into the design principles underlying the flat-direction multiscale momentum.

title: Intrinsic Interaction Geometry Controls the Low-Rank Complexity of Softmax Attention
abstract: How much matrix rank is required to preserve every bounded value output of normalized softmax attention? We study the unrestricted maximum-row-\(\ell_1\) approximation rank \(r_\varepsilon(A)\), exactly the least rank achieving uniform error over all bounded vector-valued values. Row softmax exposes the intrinsic interaction \(C=P_m(\log A)P_N\), whereas invertible \(Q/K\) gauges leave \(A\) fixed while changing the Euclidean geometry of a chosen query/key factorization. We replace that coordinate-dependent description by a projective residual \(q(C-T)\) and an attained factor-radius size \(κ(T)\). For every rank-\(r\) retained interaction with \(τ(T)<\varepsilon\), we prove $$ r_\varepsilon(A)\le \min\left\{ N,\; C_r\left( 1+\frac{κ(T)} {(\varepsilon-τ(T))^2} \right)^{r/2} \right\}, $$ with the same unknown dimension constant as the underlying weighted Gibbs-row cover. The profile is gauge invariant, termwise no worse than native retained-subspace bounds at the same declared dimension, and has a worst-case sharp \(r/2\) size exponent at fixed \(r\) and \(\varepsilon\). We then measure \(r_\varepsilon(A)\) directly on learned attention using 9,978 certified brackets across BERT, GPT-2, Qwen2.5, and two ViT checkpoints; where certificates do not close, the optimum remains interval-valued. A pre-specified 2,302-cell held-out study further shows that the historical native-coordinate geometry block contains coarse, mostly head-level information but no detectable incremental information beyond a strong calibrated baseline. The new intrinsic descriptor is not evaluated in that study. Together, the theory and measurements distinguish an operator-intrinsic complexity control from a stronger empirical explanation that the learned-head evidence does not support.

evidence.abstract: How much matrix rank is required to preserve every bounded value output of normalized softmax attention? Row softmax exposes the intrinsic interaction \(C=P_m(\log A)P_N\), whereas invertible \(Q/K\) gauges leave \(A\) fixed while changing the Euclidean geometry of a chosen query/key factorization. We replace that coordinate-dependent description by a projective residual \(q(C-T)\) and an attained factor-radius size \(κ(T)\). For every rank-\(r\) retained interaction with \(τ(T)<\varepsilon\), we prove $$ r_\varepsilon(A)\le \min\left\{ N,\; C_r\left( 1+\frac{κ(T)} {(\varepsilon-τ(T))^2} \right)^{r/2} \right\}, $$ with the same unknown dimension constant as the underlying weighted Gibbs-row cover. The profile is gauge invariant, termwise no worse than native retained-subspace bounds at the same declared dimension, and has a worst-case sharp \(r/2\) size exponent at fixed \(r\) and \(\varepsilon\). We then measure \(r_\varepsilon(A)\) directly on learned attention using 9,978 certified brackets across BERT, GPT-2, Qwen2.5, and two ViT checkpoints; where certificates do not close, the optimum remains interval-valued. A pre-specified 2,302-cell held-out study further shows that the historical native-coordinate geometry block contains coarse, mostly head-level information but no detectable incremental information beyond a strong calibrated baseline. The new intrinsic descriptor is not evaluated in that study. Together, the theory and measurements distinguish an operator-intrinsic complexity control from a stronger empirical explanation that the learned-head evidence does not support.

title: Scraping the shadows: Deep learning breakthroughs in dark web intelligence
abstract: Darknet markets (DNMs) facilitate the trade of illegal goods on a global scale. Gathering data on DNMs is critical to ensuring law enforcement agencies can effectively combat crime. Manually extracting data from DNMs is an error-prone and time-consuming task. Aiming to automate this process we develop a framework for extracting data from DNMs and evaluate the application of three state-of-the-art Named Entity Recognition (NER) models, ELMo-BiLSTM (Shah et al., 2022), UniversalNER (Zhou et al., 2023), and GLiNER (Zaratiana et al., 2024), at the task of extracting complex entities from DNM product listing pages. We propose a new annotated dataset, which we use to train, fine-tune, and evaluate the models. Our findings show that state-of-the-art NER models perform well in information extraction from DNMs, achieving 91% Precision, 96% Recall, and an F1 score of 94%. In addition, fine-tuning enhances model performance, with UniversalNER achieving the best performance.

title: Impact of Domain-Specific Intermediate Tasks on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does intermediate-task training with domain-specific English tasks (e.g., legal, medical) affect zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R's domain-specific datasets compared to general-domain intermediate tasks? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 7.8/10.

title: Majax Messenger, Beyond End-to-End Encryption. Five ML-KEM-1024 Engines Supporting a Renewable Cryptographic Architecture
abstract: Majax Messenger presents a secure messaging architecture built around defense in depth, non-residency of messages, cryptographic domain separation, daily key rotation, and five independent ML-KEM-1024 engines dedicated to messages, voice, media, real-time calls, and device identity. The system combines authenticated transport, the Maurice HMAC-based request protocol, Signal session dynamics, authenticated symmetric encryption, and post-quantum key encapsulation. This white paper describes the public architecture, measurable security properties, controlled transition between cryptographic epochs, and benchmark results while deliberately withholding operational secrets and attack-enabling implementation details. The deposit contains the English reference edition and a complete French translation. A public single-engine ML-KEM-1024 demonstrator now complements the paper at https://github.com/MajidNIMAR/majax-mlkem1024-demo. It provides source code, a Docker source build, ephemeral test keys, reciprocal encapsulation and decapsulation, negative tests, verification scripts, security documentation and SPDX SBOM generation. The demonstrator is isolated from the operational Majax architecture and is not presented as an audit or certification.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance often plateaus when faced with problems that require multiple layers of abstraction and complex relationships. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Reinforcement, designed to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to integrate SR with an evolutionary reinforcement learning (ERL) agent. The ERL agent dynamically explores the search space by generating symbolic expressions at different levels of abstraction, guided by a reward signal based on the fitness of the expressions to the data. This hierarchical structure allows the system to effectively capture intricate dependencies and ultimately produce more accurate and insightful mathematical models. The proposed method demonstrates a significant improvement in tackling complex, hierarchical regression problems compared to traditional SR techniques. The key innovation lies in the ability of the ERL agent to learn optimal levels of abstraction and strategically guide the symbolic regression process, leading to enhanced expressive power and improved solution quality.

title: SISTEM BERBASIS ATURAN DENGAN FORWARD CHAINING UNTUK REKOMENDASI LATIHAN BASKET
abstract: Latihan fisik merupakan faktor penting dalam menunjang performa pemain basket, namun kebutuhan latihan yang lebih bervariasi tergantung pada posisi mereka, pengalaman berlatih, kondisi fisik, tujuan latihan, fasilitas, waktu berlatih, dan catatan cedera. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menciptakan sistem berbasis web yang memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik bagi pemain basket dengan menggunakan metode forward chaining. Sistem ini dibangun menggunakan framework Django dan menggunakan pengetahuan berbentuk rule yang mencakup rule level, rule BMI, rule penyesuaian, rule paket latihan, dan rule cedera. Masukkan dari pengguna akan diolah sebagai fakta awal untuk menetapkan level pemain, kategori BMI, penyesuaian latihan, serta rekomendasi paket latihan yang tepat. Penelitian ini untuk menunjukan bahwa sistem BASKETEXPERT dapat memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik yang disesuaikan dengan kondisi pengguna, termasuk paket latihan utama, rekomendasi tambahan untuk BMI, penyesuaian akibat cedera, dan alasan dibalik rekomendasi tersebut. Pengujian dilakukan melalui 6 skenario dengan menggunakan metrik untuk mengevaluasi persentase kecocokan sistem. Hasil pengujian mengungkapkan bahwa 5 dari 6 skenario berfungsi dengan baik, menghasilkan persentase cocok sebesar 83,3%. Dengan demikian, sistem ini dapat berfungsi sebagai alat awal yang efektif untuk memberikan rekomendasi latihan fisik bagi pemain basket, meskipun masih dibutuhkan pengembangan lebih lanjut untuk mengatasi rule yang belum ada.

title: Нейросетевой стекинг для прогнозирования убытков в страховании
abstract: В работе раскрываются основные ограничений древовидных систем принятия решений в страховании – чувствительность к шуму и выбросам, склонность к переобучению, ограниченная способность к обобщению. Предлагаются способы их преодоления за счет методов машинного обучения, нейронных сетей и методов стекинг-ансамблирования. Ставится гипотеза о улучшении качества прогнозирования убытков, где прогнозы от нескольких базовых моделей (XGBoost, CatBoost, LogisticRegression, RandomForest, TabTransformer), в совокупности с исходными признаками набора данных, объединяются в более сильный ансамбль моделей, где строится метамодель на основе полносвязной нейронной сети с дополнительным входом исходным признаков. На данных страхования автомобилей в России за 2023-2025 годы, проводится исследование, где описывается порядок эксперимента с обучением разнородных моделей машинного обучения и нейронных сетей. Описывается алгоритм предобработки набора данных с акцентом на специфичное кодирование категорий (европейская классификация автомобилей по сегменту люксовости), делается акцент на несбалансированности целевого класса – менее 3% убытков во всем объеме данных. На основе обученных моделей строятся модели ансамблей, используя пять методов стекинг-ансамблирования: Simple Average, LogisticRegression-Constraint, Adaptive Regression by Mixing, ARM-Tweedie, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Проводится качественное сравнение базовых моделей с ансамблями моделей на основе классификационных (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) и вероятностных метрик (Logloss, BrierScore). По результатам исследования лучшей базовой моделью является TabTransformer (BrierScore = 0.037, LogLoss = 0.185, ROC-AUC = 0.635, PR-AUC = 0.054). Ансамбль на основе полносвязной нейронной сети (MLP) превзошел ее по всем ключевым метрикам (BrierScore = 0.026, LogLoss = 0.131, ROC-AUC = 0.649, PR-AUC = 0.055). Полученный результат исследования позволяют подтвердить поставленную гипотезу: ансамбль на основе полносвязной нейронной сети позволил получить прирост по основным метрикам оценки. Полученный результат доказывает методологическую ценность подхода, даже в условиях ограниченного сигнала данных нейросетевой ансамбль в совокупности с исходными признаками обеспечивает более эффективное объединение прогнозов по сравнению с методами предиктивной аналитики и методами стекинг-ансамблирования. This study examines the primary limitations of tree-based decision models in the insurance sector, namely their sensitivity to noise and outliers, susceptibility to overfitting, and limited generalization capabilities. To overcome these challenges, we propose leveraging advanced machine learning techniques, neural networks, and stacking ensemble methods. We hypothesize that the quality of loss prediction can be slightly improved by combining the predictions of multiple base models (XGBoost, CatBoost, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and TabTransformer), alongside the original dataset features, into a more robust ensemble. Specifically, the meta-model is constructed as a fully connected neural network with an additional input layer for the original features. The empirical study utilizes Russian auto insurance data from 2023 to 2025, detailing the experimental framework for training heterogeneous machine learning and neural network models. The data preprocessing pipeline is described, with a particular focus on a specific categorical encoding scheme based on the European car classification by luxury segment. Special attention is given to the severe imbalance of the target class, as losses account for less than 3% of the total dataset. Based on the trained base models, ensemble models are constructed using five stacking techniques: Simple Average, Constrained Logistic Regression, Adaptive Regression by Mixing (ARM), ARM-Tweedie, and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). A comprehensive comparative analysis of the base models and the ensembles is conducted using both classification metrics (ROC-AUC, PR-AUC) and probabilistic metrics (Log Loss, Brier Score). The results indicate that the best-performing base model is TabTransformer (Brier Score = 0.037, Log Loss = 0.185, ROC-AUC = 0.635, PR-AUC = 0.054). The MLP-based ensemble outperformed it across all key metrics (Brier Score = 0.026, Log Loss = 0.131, ROC-AUC = 0.649, PR-AUC = 0.055). These findings confirm the initial hypothesis: the fully connected neural network ensemble yields a slightly improvement in the primary evaluation metrics. This demonstrates the methodological value of the proposed approach: even under conditions of a weak data signal, the neural network ensemble, augmented with original features, ensures a more effective aggregation of predictions compared to traditional predictive analytics and alternative stacking ensemble methods.

title: Posthoc Explainability Models
abstract: For complex models such as deep neural networks, explainability is not available intrinsically. The explanations have to be derived from the models using well-defined XAI methods that are called “Post-hoc Explainability Models.” To make predictions with a neural network, the data input is passed through many layers of multiplication with the learned weights and through nonlinear transformations. A single prediction can involve millions of mathematical operations depending on the architecture of the neural network. There is no chance that we humans can follow the exact mapping from data input to prediction. We would have to consider millions of weights that interact in a complex way to understand a prediction by a neural network. To interpret the behavior and predictions of neural networks, we need specific interpretation methods, and they are nothing but the “Post-hoc Explainability Models.”

title: How do the attributes of AI-generated digital humans relate to online customer experience? Evidence from SEM and fsQCA
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how AI-generated digital human attributes relate to online customer experience, identifies the configurational pathways linked to shared online customer experience, extends the research boundaries of generative AI in marketing, and expands the body of literature concerning online customer experience. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative online questionnaire was distributed to consumers with AI digital human interaction experience, collecting 607 valid responses for subsequent statistical analysis. This study draws on affordance theory to conceptualise four key attributes of AI-generated digital humans. A mixed-analytical design integrating structural equation modelling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) is adopted to examine variable associations, mediating linkages, and multi-factor configurational pathways. title: Satellite‐Based Global Assessment of Solar Resource Stability
abstract: Abstract Satellite spatial smoothing complicates comparisons of solar variability between gridded products and point measurements. We introduce the Stability Deviation Index (SDI), a bounded composite of solar intensity and intraday variability. Applied independently to 69 BSRN stations and co‐located CERES grid cells, SDI shows strong cross‐platform agreement ( R = 0.89, mean bias ≈0). Applying SDI to 23 years of CERES satellite records (2001–2023) reveals an obvious climatic divergence: stable subtropical regions are becoming more stable, while coastal and equatorial zones are becoming more volatile. Overlaying SDI maps with global PV inventories reveals a systematic spatial mismatch between PV deployment patterns and climatic stability. Although utility‐scale plants are optimally located, over 70% of small‐scale distributed PV systems are deployed in highly volatile regions, particularly in China and India. Ultimately, SDI translates smoothed Earth observations into actionable, grid‐compatible intelligence, highlighting hidden systemic risks in modern solar deployment.

title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
abstract: Steering with Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offers a lightweight inference-time path for adapting the behavior of large language models without retraining. By exposing sparse and interpretable features, SAE steering provides a promising interface for safety control that guides harmful continuations toward refusal. However, we observe that complex wrappers can still undermine existing SAE steering methods on harmful prompts. To evaluate this failure mode systematically, we construct Generalized Undercover Instruction Safety Evaluation (GUISE), a dataset of harmful prompts with complex wrappers. Existing single direction SAE steering methods do not reliably produce refusals on harmful prompts, suggesting that refusal enhancement alone can be too weak when the harmful continuation path remains active. This motivates us to propose Refusal-Enhanced INhibitory Steering (REINS), which suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features in the same SAE feature space. Experiments on GUISE and other datasets show that prior methods either intervene too weakly or achieve only apparent safety through collapse, while REINS substantially reduces harmful responses, markedly improves safe refusals and largely preserves general capabilities.

title: Exploring the Design Space of Representation Learning for Audio Transformations
abstract: Neural audio representation learning has enabled a range of content-oriented applications, but the resulting features remain limited for tasks involving audio processing. Furthermore, it is not obvious what processing-aware representations should capture: the processing itself, abstracted away from source content, or the processed audio that retains it. Existing approaches implicitly commit to one or the other and also differ in their models, data, and evaluation, obscuring which design choices drive their behavior. We address both questions within a unified framework of three objectives: processing consistency, description alignment, and equivariance via forward prediction. We compare all combinations of the objectives under a controlled setup and reveal their relative strengths and interactions. Our framework produces both a transformation embedding and a processed-audio embedding, and we find that the two play complementary roles: distance-based tasks favor the former, while probe-based tasks favor the latter. Combined with improvements in network architecture and training pipeline, our representations outperform prior baselines across retrieval, probe-based evaluation, and style transfer.

title: SimpCue: Cue-Based Prompting for Multilingual Text Simplification
abstract: Text simplification aims to make complex texts easier to understand while preserving their original meaning. Recent large language models can perform simplification through prompting, but it remains unclear whether adding explicit linguistic information about sentence complexity to the prompt improves their outputs. We investigate this question for multilingual sentence-level Easy-to-Read simplification in Catalan, Spanish, and Italian. Using Qwen3-8B, we compare a baseline prompt, a gold-cue prompt enriched with gold linguistic cues, and a predicted-cue prompt enriched with automatically predicted cues. We evaluate the outputs using SARI, BLEU, chrF, and BERTScore, and complement this evaluation with a manual qualitative analysis. Predicted-cue prompting obtains the best overall scores across all four metrics, although the gains over the baseline are small. Gold-cue prompting does not consistently improve over the baseline, and results vary across languages. These findings indicate that cue-based prompting can influence multilingual Easy-to-Read simplification, but its benefits are modest, metric-dependent, and language-dependent.

title: Serialization Order Confounds Attention Analysis in MeshXL
abstract: Autoregressive mesh transformers look like an unusually convenient target for mechanistic interpretability: the token stream is the geometry, so every attention weight has a literal spatial address and can be painted onto the surface being generated. We show that this convenience is a trap. In MeshXL's canonical serialization, faces arrive sorted by height, so a face's index in the token stream predicts its vertical position at Spearman rho = 0.951 across all 2820 training chairs, and a cubic in normalized sequence position explains 86% of height variance. Any attention map read spatially is therefore confounded with plain recency. The confound is structural rather than incidental: it is a property of the preprocessing, its median across four object categories ranges only from +0.914 to +0.968, and re-ordering faces to break it raises cross-entropy fortyfold on every mesh tested. Controlling for sequence position on unmodified inputs, attention's partial correlation with 3D proximity is +0.194 (95% CI [+0.165, +0.206]) against +0.430 for sequence proximity; the spatial estimate replicates at +0.180 ([+0.167, +0.199]) on a disjoint held-out sample. No head in the network is primarily geometric, none reaching rho_spatial = 0.50 while rho_seq reaches +0.951, and layers 0-11 carry no geometric selectivity at all. Testing mesh topology, a geometric feature nearly independent of the confound, attention does not track it (+0.041, no head above +0.15), while sensitivity to repeated coordinate tokens between non-touching faces is twice as strong. Separately, MeshXL inherits OPT-1.3b's transformer body and reinitializes only its embeddings; we find its attention sinks bear no relation to OPT's (rho = -0.146) while being sevenfold stronger, so they form under mesh training rather than arriving with the weights. All confirmatory claims follow rules fixed before any attention was extracted. Of three such arms, one returned inconclusive, one failed its own validity gate, and one was refuted; all three are reported as they landed.
