title: Human-machine collaborative deductive program synthesis
abstract: Traditional approaches used for deductive program synthesis provide high accuracy of problem analysis and solution generation. However, in order to comprehend and interpret solutions, they require extensive knowledge and thorough understanding of formal logic. This creates a significant barrier between human logic and its implementation in synthesis programs using the deductive approach. This paper proposes a novel human-machine collaborative approach to deductive program synthesis that leverages the mutual strengths of human intuition and advanced logical computation. Our methodology integrates human problem formulation, its automated formalization via large language models, and human verification of the problem, machine-driven program synthesis based on constructive inference, their execution, and iterative feedbacks during the program synthesis. We demonstrate the practical applicability of this approach through an illustrative case study: that is inferring product-manufacturing technologies from a database that is producing and processing the information at the same time. This framework holds the potential for humans to democratize access to powerful formal methods and accelerate the development of complex, logically sound software solutions.

title: CITADEL-Series Software Feasibility Experiments: DON26BZ05-DV082 (CIT-001 through CIT-014)
abstract: 14 preregistered software feasibility experiments conducted on August 28, 2026, for the Cross-domain Interface for Trusted Access and Data Exchange Logic (CITADEL) topic (DON26BZ05-DV082), Department of the Navy SBIR FY26 Round 5. All 14 experiments matched their preregistered predictions. Includes a remediation experiment (CIT-011b) demonstrating 503.55 Mbps content-parsing throughput on 10,000 mixed frames (288,625,000 payload bytes). Conducted using a containerized Python harness implementing the ExecutionProof four-engine decision pipeline (Authority, Evidence, Constraint, Control) with bidirectional cross-domain policy enforcement across four simulated enclaves. This series is maintained as a separate corpus from the 106-experiment general ExecutionProof design-before-execution corpus. Also includes the preregistration document for CIT-015 through CIT-018 (not yet executed).

title: Graph Representation Learning: Leveraging Topological Sensitivity
abstract: Graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful technique for analyzing and understanding complex data structures represented as graphs. Traditional methods often overlook the inherent topological information embedded within these graphs, leading to suboptimal representations. This research investigates the influence of topological sensitivity in graph representation learning and proposes a novel learning algorithm designed to effectively utilize graph topology. The core claim is that the topological structure of a graph significantly impacts its representation, necessitating methods that explicitly incorporate this information. We explore the use of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Graph Attention Networks (GATs) to integrate topological features, combined with optimization strategies based on degree centrality and other topological metrics. The results demonstrate a marked improvement in representation quality and learning efficiency when topological sensitivity is deliberately addressed. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of graph representation learning and offers a practical approach for enhancing its performance across diverse applications.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Improvement Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper investigates improvements to Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. The core claim centers on optimizing the decoherence process to enhance the security and key generation rate of QKD systems. This is achieved through a detailed analysis of the underlying physical mechanisms governing decoherence and the subsequent design of a novel decoherence suppression technique aimed at minimizing the decoherence time of quantum states. The proposed approach addresses a critical limitation in existing QKD protocols – the vulnerability to decoherence – while simultaneously boosting key generation efficiency. The theoretical framework presented demonstrates a significant potential for increased security and higher key rates, offering a pathway towards more robust and practical quantum cryptography. Mathematical models are presented to illustrate the key concepts and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method. The investigation focuses on the theoretical aspects of the protocol improvement, without experimental validation.

title: Quantum Acceleration of Machine Learning via Entanglement Decay
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging entanglement decay, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, to accelerate machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with noisy data and require significant computational resources, particularly for complex models and large datasets. We propose a hardware-accelerated approach that exploits entanglement decay to mitigate noise and enhance the accuracy of computations. The core idea involves translating key steps within a machine learning algorithm into a quantum circuit, where the controlled decay of entanglement acts as a built-in error correction mechanism. We outline a novel computational model and discuss the theoretical considerations and challenges associated with implementing such a system. Specifically, we explore how the rate of entanglement decay can be tuned to optimize the algorithm's performance and robustness. This work aims to provide a foundational understanding of using quantum decoherence for hardware-level machine learning acceleration.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Semantic Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical expressions that accurately represent a given dataset. Traditional symbolic regression methods, while effective in finding optimal expressions, often struggle to produce models that are truly interpretable or semantically meaningful. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Semantic Constraints, designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to build a hierarchical system for expression generation, where symbolic expressions are constructed at multiple levels of abstraction. Crucially, this system incorporates "semantic constraints" – rules derived from domain knowledge – to guide the regression process toward expressions that are not only accurate but also conceptually understandable. The proposed method significantly improves the interpretability of symbolic regression results and offers the potential for more efficient model discovery. We outline the architecture of the system, detailing the hierarchical structure and the mechanism for integrating semantic constraints. The key innovation lies in the proactive guidance provided by domain knowledge, shifting the focus from purely numerical optimization to a more informed, semantically driven search. The results, while presented conceptually due to the absence of experimental validation, demonstrate the potential of this approach to yield more understandable and useful symbolic models.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Simulation of Complex Systems with Unknown Parameters
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) for modeling and simulating complex systems characterized by numerous unknown parameters. Traditional approaches to modeling such systems often struggle with effectively representing and quantifying the inherent uncertainty associated with these unknowns. PPLs offer a novel solution by allowing the explicit incorporation of prior knowledge, uncertain parameter values, and their resulting probabilistic relationships within a single, declarative framework. We demonstrate how this approach facilitates robust uncertainty quantification through simulation, enabling exploration of a system's behavior under various parameter assumptions. The core claim is that PPLs provide a powerful tool for modeling and simulating complex systems with unknown parameters, allowing for robust uncertainty quantification. The paper details the core mechanism of utilizing a PPL to define a system model and perform simulations to quantify uncertainty. This work highlights the increased flexibility and expressiveness of PPLs compared to conventional modeling techniques.

title: Based Topological Optimization of Quantum Circuit Design Method
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for optimizing quantum circuit design utilizing topological optimization techniques. The core idea revolves around representing quantum circuits as topological networks and employing topological optimization algorithms to refine their structure. This approach aims to minimize the number of quantum gates required, thereby enhancing the efficiency and scalability of quantum computation. The research explores the potential of this method to significantly reduce circuit complexity and improve overall performance. The primary contribution lies in the application of topological optimization to the inherently complex domain of quantum circuit design, offering a potentially transformative approach to quantum computing. Mathematical formulations and key concepts are presented to illustrate the method's principles and demonstrate its feasibility.

title: Self-Supervised Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding and Graph Structure
abstract: This paper proposes a novel self-supervised learning framework that combines Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) with graph-structured information. The core idea is to enhance the predictive capabilities of CPC by explicitly modeling relationships between data points. We hypothesize that incorporating graph structure will improve the quality of learned representations, especially for datasets exhibiting inherent relational dependencies. The method leverages the inherent predictive nature of CPC, where a network learns to predict future representations based on past ones. By adding a graph structure, we encourage the network to learn dependencies between nodes, thereby improving the accuracy of predictions and ultimately, the quality of the learned representations. The framework is presented with detailed mathematical formulations and a clear explanation of the integration process. The results, though not presented through experimental validation due to the focus on the theoretical framework, suggest a significant potential for improvement in representation learning tasks when graph structure is incorporated.

title: Contextualized Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Neural Network Embeddings
abstract: Probabilistic programming (PP) offers a powerful approach to modeling uncertainty and performing inference. However, a significant challenge remains in effectively incorporating complex, real-world data distributions, particularly those exhibiting high dimensionality and intricate dependencies. This work proposes a novel framework that addresses this limitation by directly embedding Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) into probabilistic programming languages. title: Beyond Vector Search: Comparing Classical RAG with Hybrid GraphRAG for Climate Science Q\&A
abstract: Traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems treat documents in isolation, failing to capture hierarchical relationships between concepts in complex scientific corpora. This limitation compromises answer quality in specialized domains such as climatology, where conceptual dependencies frequently traverse multiple articles. We propose a hybrid architecture that integrates vector search with GraphRAG, Leiden community detection, and cross-encoder re-ranking, achieving gains of 160\% in contextual relevance and 177\% in contextual recall compared to classical RAG. These results demonstrate that unifying local and global retrieval significantly outperforms text-span isolation, paving the way for more effective question-answering systems over dispersed scientific literature.

title: PCBnet: A Dataset and Automatic Construction of SPICE Netlists from Schematic Images
abstract: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are fundamental to modern electronic systems, yet AI-driven PCB design automation remains constrained by the lack of large-scale paired schematic-netlist datasets. PCB schematics are particularly challenging due to diverse component types, complex wiring topologies, and noisy textual annotations. To address this gap, we present PCBnet, a large-scale PCB schematic dataset comprising over 300 real-world designs with annotated pins and paired SPICE netlists. It contains more than 50,000 component instances, 150,000 wires, 100,000 text regions, and 400,000 characters. We further develop an automated schematic-to-netlist pipeline that combines visual recognition, topology construction, and domain-knowledge-guided multi-agent correction. The proposed method achieves 94.54% component detection mAP, 98.57% text recognition accuracy, and 84.47% end-to-end connectivity accuracy. PCBnet provides a benchmark and data foundation for future AI-driven PCB design automation.

title: High-Throughput Normalized Min-Sum Belief Propagation Decoding for Quantum LDPC Codes with Near-Memory Processing
abstract: Real-time quantum error correction requires classical decoders to process growing syndrome workloads with low and predictable latency. For quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, iterative belief propagation (BP) repeatedly updates messages over sparse Tanner graphs, creating substantial memory-access and data-movement demands. We map normalized Min-Sum BP decoding of the [[144,12,12]] Bivariate Bicycle qLDPC code onto a DPU-based Processing-in-Memory (PIM) architecture. Within each DPU, 11 tasklets cooperatively decode one syndrome, while multiple DPUs process independent syndrome instances in parallel. Using uPIMulator and a data-qubit Pauli error model with ideal syndrome measurements, we compare throughput, per-syndrome processing time, logical error rate (LER), and single-syndrome tail latency against a 16-logical-CPU baseline. At a component-wise physical error probability of p=0.001 and one BP iteration, the projected aggregate kernel throughput of 2,560 DPUs reaches 1.071 x 10^7 decodes/s, compared with 1.22 x 10^6 decodes/s for the CPU, an 8.8x improvement. From two iterations onward, the measured LER remains below the physical error probability for every evaluated value of p. For one to five iterations, the maximum sampled serialized X+Z DPU compute latency remains below the 1 ms decoder-side reference for trapped-ion QEC, reaching approximately 0.873 ms at five iterations. These results show that near-memory processing can provide high aggregate throughput and sub-millisecond compute latency for qLDPC BP decoding under the evaluated conditions.

title: Fault‐Tolerant Quantum Simulation of the Pauli‐Breit Hamiltonian for Ab Initio Hybrid Quantum‐Classical Molecular Design With Applications to Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Relativistic spin effects are driving subtle molecular processes ranging from intersystem crossing in photodynamic therapy to spin‐mediated catalysis and high‐resolution spectroscopy. These effects can be described by the Pauli‐Breit Hamiltonian, which extends the nonrelativistic electronic Hamiltonian by including explicit one‐ and two‐electron spin‐orbit and spin‐spin interactions. However, first‐principles simulations of the full Pauli‐Breit Hamiltonian quickly become intractable on classical computers due to the rapid growth of Hilbert space dimension and the complexity of two‐body spin‐dependent terms. In this work, we propose a fault‐tolerant quantum algorithm for computing molecular energy levels and properties governed by the Pauli‐Breit Hamiltonian. The central result of the paper is an explicit block‐encoding construction for the relativistic Hamiltonian in a second‐quantized, doubly factorized representation. By reformulating the Pauli‐Breit Hamiltonian in a symmetry‐adapted Majorana basis, we construct efficient linear‐combination‐of‐unitaries circuits that encode both one‐ and two‐electron spin‐orbit coupling without resorting to effective or mean‐field approximations. We introduce spin‐controlled Pauli‐SWAP networks that decouple spin and orbital control logic, enabling a unified treatment of relativistic spin mixing with only a modest overhead relative to spin‐free electronic structure simulations. We analyze the resulting quantum resources in terms of logical qubit counts and T‐gate complexity, and show that the inclusion of spin degrees of freedom does not fundamentally worsen the asymptotic scaling. The prefactor in our approach is 2–4 lower than if the linear‐combination of unitaries technique was applied directly. The present manuscript focuses on explicit circuit constructions and scaling analysis, rather than molecule‐specific numerical resource estimates. To illustrate one prospective application, we outline a first‐principles hybrid quantum‐classical workflow for the rational design of photodynamic therapy photosensitizers, artificial photosynthesis catalysts, and other molecular systems where accurate treatment of relativistic spin effects is essential.

title: Применение субъектно-ориентированного подхода при построении онтологии учебной дисциплины
abstract: The need to rethink the key elements and general methodology of the educational process determined the relevance of this study. The purpose of the study is to find means of increasing the effectiveness of teaching in higher education through student involvement in the educational process using a subject-oriented approach. The originality of the presented material lies in its interdisciplinarity, which made it possible to apply knowledge from the field of management to solve pedagogical problems using ontological modeling tools, which resulted in a qualitatively new solution to the problem. An ontology of the subject area of the academic discipline is constructed. Some terms and concepts from the developed thesaurus of the discipline are presented. A subject-oriented approach is proposed as a methodology for constructing an ontology of the subject area of the academic discipline. A distinctive feature of the applied approach is the definition of the role of students in the development of the curriculum for the discipline (it is proposed that students supplement the work program in accordance with their individual characteristics ad hoc). It is shown how the joint activities of the teacher and students contribute to the involvement of students in the educational process and improve the effectiveness of learning. The methods used were systems analysis, logical analysis, generalization and systematization of material, and knowledge visualization.

title: Scaling Multilingual Intermediate Tasks in English-Only Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does scaling the number of multilingual intermediate tasks (e.g., 5, 10, 20) during English-only intermediate-task training impact the zero-shot cross-lingual performance (EM/F1) of LLMs on the XTREME-R benchmark across high-, mid-, and low-resource languages? title: Quantum Machine Learning for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum machine learning (QML) techniques to address complex optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with scalability and computational cost, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional or non-convex landscapes. Quantum machine learning offers a potential paradigm shift by leveraging quantum mechanics to accelerate and potentially improve the solution process. We detail a framework where optimization problems are formulated as quantum machine learning tasks, employing algorithms like Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) to tackle these problems. The core claim is that QML can significantly enhance the efficiency of optimization, offering a pathway to solve problems intractable for classical methods. We present a theoretical foundation and outline the mechanisms driving this potential improvement, focusing on the transformation of classical optimization problems into quantum-compatible formulations. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the challenges associated with realizing the full potential of QML in optimization.

title: Formalization of Intuitive Programming Concepts with Category Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of category theory to provide a rigorous and foundational framework for programming languages. Traditional programming paradigms often rely on intuitive, but sometimes inconsistent, representations of concepts like recursion and higher-order functions. This work proposes a core claim: that these concepts can be formalized more effectively by mapping them to established category theoretic constructs such as functors, natural transformations, and monads. The paper details this mapping process, illustrating how category theory's abstract mathematical approach can lead to a deeper understanding of programming and potentially inspire new paradigms. The central mechanism involves the translation of programming constructs into their category theoretic equivalents, offering a more consistent and elegant representation. The ultimate goal is to explore the possibility of designing programming languages based on these foundational category theoretic principles.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Automated Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to automate the process of algorithm design. The core idea is to frame algorithm design as a two-player game between a generator and a discriminator. The generator learns to create new algorithms, while the discriminator learns to distinguish between genuine and artificially generated algorithms. We propose a framework for training such a GAN, outlining key considerations for architecture design, loss functions, and evaluation metrics. The potential benefits of this approach – namely, automating a traditionally manual and often time-consuming process – are discussed, alongside the challenges associated with defining and evaluating algorithm novelty and effectiveness. We present a theoretical model and outline the steps involved in leveraging GANs to discover and refine algorithms for a variety of computational problems. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate that GANs can serve as a powerful tool for accelerating algorithm innovation and potentially uncovering solutions beyond human intuition.

title: Distributed Information Theory for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial for reliable quantum computation, but traditional approaches often suffer from scalability issues. This work introduces a novel distributed information theory protocol for QEC, departing from classical distributed coding paradigms. The core idea is to utilize correlated information sharing across a network of nodes, exploiting quantum entanglement to achieve greater efficiency and resilience to errors. We present a framework where the redundancy is distributed intelligently, minimizing the required resources per qubit while maintaining high correction capabilities. The protocol's performance is analyzed theoretically, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve the practicality of QEC in large-scale quantum systems. We explore the key mathematical concepts underpinning this approach, including the distribution of quantum states, the quantification of information, and the analysis of error propagation within the distributed network. The theoretical analysis focuses on characterizing the rate of information transfer and the fidelity of the corrected state, providing a framework for optimizing the protocol's parameters.

title: Topological Optimization of Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper investigates the topological optimization of quantum error correction codes, aiming to enhance their error-correcting performance and coding efficiency. We propose a novel approach leveraging topological protection principles to design an error-correcting code and subsequently optimize its topological structure. The core mechanism involves manipulating the code's topology to mitigate the effects of local errors and improve overall resilience. Through careful analysis and mathematical formulation, we demonstrate that optimized topological structures lead to significant improvements in error correction capabilities. The specific focus is on tailoring the code's connectivity and redundancy to achieve a better balance between error protection and the overhead associated with encoding. This work contributes to the advancement of practical quantum error correction by providing a framework for systematically designing and optimizing topological codes. The primary goal is to achieve higher fidelity quantum computations by reducing the impact of noise.

title: AOA-Constrained, Calibrated Random-Forest Prospectivity Mapping for Au-Ag in Nevada Great Basin: Spatially Independent Validation, Uncertainty, and Decision-Focused Top-k Targets
abstract: Mineral prospectivity mapping (MPM) increasingly relies on machine learning classifiers, but model performance may be overstated when spatial dependence, extrapolation beyond the training domain, and poorly calibrated prediction scores are not adequately addressed. This study presents a reproducible workflow for regional Au-Ag prospectivity mapping in Nevada that integrates positive–unlabeled learning with Random Forest models and spatial GroupKFold cross-validation. Predictions were restricted to the Area of Applicability (AOA), defined using the 0.95 quantile of a training-derived feature-space dissimilarity index, resulting in areal coverage of 54.331% for Ag and 73.118% for Au. Discrimination based on pooled out-of-fold (OOF) predictions was strong for both commodities (Ag:AP = 0.745, ROC-AUC = 0.908; Au:AP = 0.777, ROC-AUC = 0.912). Post hoc OOF calibration with isotonic regression reduced Brier scores and improved probability reliability within the supported prediction domain. Area-based validation showed that the highest-ranked 10% of the AOA captured 85.6% of the Ag and 84.2% of the Au pooled-OOF positives, corresponding to targeting efficiencies of 8.6-fold and 8.4-fold relative to random spatial selection. Ensemble dispersion was used to map predictive uncertainty and to identify areas where additional data may be most useful for reducing uncertainty. SHAP importance and partial-dependence diagnostics consistently highlighted proximity to Quaternary faults, elevated slip and dilation tendency, and potential-field edges associated with intrusive or volcanic contacts, while surface heat flow acted mainly as a permissive control. The resulting AOA-masked prospectivity maps, uncertainty layers, and top-k targeting products provide a transparent regional framework for prioritizing follow-up exploration and allocating reconnaissance effort.

title: TK ‐ SMF : Top‐K Semantic Mask Fusion With Dynamic Budget and Recovery Against Adversarial Patch Attacks Under Semantic Fragmentation in Vision Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep learning‐based vision models have severe security vulnerabilities against physical adversarial patch attacks. Previous studies propose explainability‐based defense mechanisms (e.g., PatchOut and SALIUITL). These methods aim to recover the system by masking the regions that affect model decisions the most. However, these approaches generally assume that the adversarial effect is located in a single, continuous region (single mask selection). In this study, we empirically demonstrate the “Semantic Fragmentation” and saliency bleeding problems caused by multiple scattered patches in explainability maps. To overcome this issue, we propose the “Top‐K Semantic Mask Fusion with Dynamic Budget (TK‐SMF)” system. The proposed framework initially extracts explainability maps using LayerGradCAM, subsequently constructs a pool of candidate semantic segments via the Fast Segment Anything Model (FastSAM), and ultimately fuses the Top‐K highest‐risk masks within a strictly fixed area budget. This budget is anchored to a predefined worst‐case threat assumption, eliminating the need to know the attacker's actual patch count during inference. We then restore the selected masked areas using OpenCV Inpainting to achieve model recovery. We evaluated the proposed framework on 38 distinct and challenging physical‐world scenarios, encompassing diverse tactical vehicle categories under single‐ and multipatch attacks. Experimental results prove that TK‐SMF breaks the targeted attack illusion with a 100% success rate. evidence.title: TK ‐ SMF : Top‐K Semantic Mask Fusion With Dynamic Budget and Recovery Against Adversarial Patch Attacks Under Semantic Fragmentation in Vision Models
evidence.abstract: ABSTRACT Deep learning‐based vision models have severe security vulnerabilities against physical adversarial patch attacks. Previous studies propose explainability‐based defense mechanisms (e.g., PatchOut and SALIUITL). These methods aim to recover the system by masking the regions that affect model decisions the most. However, these approaches generally assume that the adversarial effect is located in a single, continuous region (single mask selection). In this study, we empirically demonstrate the “Semantic Fragmentation” and saliency bleeding problems caused by multiple scattered patches in explainability maps. To overcome this issue, we propose the “Top‐K Semantic Mask Fusion with Dynamic Budget (TK‐SMF)” system. The proposed framework initially extracts explainability maps using LayerGradCAM, subsequently constructs a pool of candidate semantic segments via the Fast Segment Anything Model (FastSAM), and ultimately fuses the Top‐K highest‐risk masks within a strictly fixed area budget. This budget is anchored to a predefined worst‐case threat assumption, eliminating the need to know the attacker's actual patch count during inference. We then restore the selected masked areas using OpenCV Inpainting to achieve model recovery. We evaluated the proposed framework on 38 distinct and challenging physical‐world scenarios, encompassing diverse tactical vehicle categories under single‐ and multipatch attacks. Experimental results prove that TK‐SMF breaks the targeted attack illusion with a 100% success rate. The results show that dynamic and flexible defense architectures exceed the limits of the single‐mask assumption. They significantly improve model accuracy and reliability against complex physical world threats.

title: SABER: Stability-Aware Early Exit for LLM Reasoning via Adversarial Branch Probing
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) achieve strong reasoning capabilities, yet long-chain reasoning becomes inefficient once the intermediate answer stabilizes across reasoning steps: additional reasoning yields little marginal benefit while incurring substantial inference cost. Existing early-exit methods based on confidence or entropy poorly capture reasoning stability, while consistency-based approaches rely on multi-step trajectory agreement, requiring sequential evaluations that delay exit. To better balance efficiency and reliability, we propose SABER, a training-free framework for stability-aware early exit via adversarial branch probing. SABER constructs simple yet effective semantic perturbations around intermediate reasoning states to form adversarial branches, and applies lightweight probing to estimate their likely final outcomes without full trajectory rollouts. When the probed outcomes remain consistent across branches, SABER exits early; otherwise, it continues reasoning. Experiments across multiple reasoning benchmarks and model architectures show that SABER reduces reasoning token consumption by 30.2\%--39.8\% on average while maintaining competitive accuracy with full-length reasoning.

title: ITER: Interaction-Aware Retrieval for Agentic Search
abstract: Deep-research agents answer complex user questions through an iterative sequence of search steps, where the agent autonomously formulates sub-queries to retrieve the evidence needed at each stage. However, existing retriever training typically relies only on the sub-query and its corresponding search results at the current step as training signals, leaving the information accumulated from previous interactions largely underutilized. We introduce iter, an agent interaction-aware dense retriever trained using agent trajectory learning signals. iter represents each query by incorporating not only the current sub-query, but also the main question and preceding sub-queries, and is trained using trajectory-relative learning signals derived from the agent's interactions. Across six agent backbones from three model families, iter consistently outperforms the existing agent-trajectory-trained dense retriever, LRAT, achieving an average improvement of 7.5% on InfoSeek-Eval and 13.5% on BrowseComp-Plus. iter also demonstrates stronger cross-agent robustness than AgentIR, a deep-research retriever that relies on external LLM-judge signals and the agent's pre-search reasoning. Ablations further show that the main question and previous sub-queries provide the most robust query representation, while previously visited and useful documents, used as redundancy negatives in subsequent searches, provide the strongest trajectory-relative supervision. Code is available at https://github.com/ielab/ITER.

title: Оценка объяснений моделей «чёрного ящика» посредством интеграции метода взвешенной суммы на основе Z-чисел
abstract: The problem of objective comparison of the quality of explanations produced by explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods is considered. A multi-method evaluation scheme is proposed. It combines four automatically computable metrics, five human-centered criteria, and an integration procedure into a single rank. The fidelity of an explanation is computed as the posterior Bayesian probability of its consistency with the model decision. In-formativeness is assessed by a weighted fuzzy mean of the membership degrees of semantic properties. Stability is measured by the Jaccard coefficient and the Euclidean distance. Partial scores are aggregated by a Z-number-based weighted sum mod-el. Criteria weights are computed by the eigenvector method applied to a Z-valued pairwise comparison matrix. The reliability component of a Z-number reflects the credibility of each measurement and reduces the contribution of degenerate scores. The scheme is validated by comparing eight XAI approaches on the German Credit Risk dataset. The comparison includes SHAP, LIME, counterfactual explanations, fuzzy rules, fuzzy decision trees, and three ontology-based approaches. The quantitative and human-centered rankings are consistent. The Spearman rank correlation between them is 0.86. In both loops, the highest integral rank was obtained by the fuzzy semantic approach built on Fuzzy OWL2. The result demonstrates the discriminative power of the scheme and its applicability to arbitrary XAI methods.

title: Explainability-First Workforce Risk Assessment for Industrial Automation: SHAP Attributions, Permutation Importance, Cross-Method Convergence, and Legal Compliance Framework
abstract: Abstract: Regulatory requirements (ЎРҚ-819 Art.37, ПҚ-358-сон) mandate interpretable, auditable explanations for ML models in industrial control contexts. This paper applies SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation importance to a logistic regression attrition predictor (n=1,470) integrated into an APCS. OverTime_Yes dominates all methods (mean|SHAP|=0.617). Cross-method Spearman ρ=0.918 confirms explanation robustness. A 15-feature importance hierarchy is established for the operator dashboard. Eight-subgroup fairness audit confirms gender parity (TPR: female=0.583, male=0.567). A seven-layer responsible architecture maps every component to its Uzbekistan legal obligation (ЗРУ-547, ЎРҚ-819, ПҚ-358-сон, ЗРУ-798). Keywords: Explainable AI; SHAP; permutation importance; workforce risk; fairness; responsible automation; industrial control; regulatory compliance.

title: Dynamic Coreference Resolution via Predictive Latent Variable Models
abstract: Coreference resolution, the task of identifying all expressions referring to the same entity in a text, is a fundamental problem in natural language understanding. Traditional coreference resolution systems often rely on static rules and hand-crafted features, limiting their ability to handle the complexities and ambiguities inherent in natural language. This paper introduces a novel approach to coreference resolution based on predictive latent variable models. Our system leverages a probabilistic model to dynamically represent coreference relationships, incorporating both local contextual information and a set of hidden latent variables that capture global semantic dependencies. The predictive nature of the model allows it to adapt its coreference predictions as new information becomes available, leading to improved accuracy, particularly in scenarios with ambiguous contextual cues. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a detailed analysis and theoretical framework, highlighting its advantages over existing static models. The core of our system lies in the dynamic adjustment of the latent state, enabling a more nuanced understanding of coreference relationships. This work contributes to the advancement of coreference resolution by providing a flexible and robust framework capable of handling the inherent uncertainties of natural language.

title: Design of a Quantum Computing Architecture Based on Multi-Scale Quantum Field Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computing architecture design, leveraging the principles of multi-scale quantum field theory (MSQFT). Traditional quantum computing architectures often face challenges in precise control and efficient inter-qubit connectivity due to their reliance on simplified models. We argue that a quantum computing system can be effectively treated as a multi-scale quantum field theory system. This framework allows us to utilize the powerful tools of field theory for rigorous modeling and analysis, ultimately leading to more accurate qubit design and control strategies. The core claim is the establishment of a methodology for designing quantum computing architectures based on MSQFT, enabling precise control and efficient qubit connections. The proposed mechanism involves translating quantum computing requirements into field theory formulations, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to conventional finite element methods. This work outlines the key concepts and provides a theoretical foundation for developing sophisticated quantum computing architectures with enhanced performance and scalability. The presented architecture aims to overcome limitations inherent in traditional approaches by incorporating the inherent complexity and multi-scale nature of quantum systems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Exploration-Exploitation Tradeoff
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) faces a persistent challenge in effectively managing the exploration-exploitation tradeoff. Traditional RL methods often rely on heuristics or simplified models, leading to suboptimal performance. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming to address this limitation. We introduce a framework where the agent's policy is explicitly represented as a probability distribution over actions, enabling the incorporation of Bayesian optimization techniques for a more nuanced and principled exploration-exploitation balance. This approach allows for dynamic adaptation of exploration based on observed rewards and uncertainties, moving beyond fixed exploration strategies. The key contribution lies in the ability to directly model the tradeoff within the probabilistic framework, facilitating more efficient learning and improved performance in complex RL environments. We demonstrate the potential of this method through theoretical analysis and outline a framework for future research and development.

title: Self-Correcting Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Descent
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic programming, termed "Self-Correcting Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Descent." The core challenge in probabilistic programming lies in selecting the optimal inference algorithm for a given problem. Traditional Bayesian methods often rely on fixed algorithms that may not adapt to the specific characteristics of the model or data, leading to suboptimal results and the inherent limitations of the "no-free-lunch theorem." Our proposed system addresses this issue by integrating a dynamic Bayesian descent algorithm that continuously monitors and corrects its own performance. This self-correcting mechanism adapts the algorithm's learning rate and exploration strategy based on metrics such as posterior variance, effectively creating a self-optimizing inference engine. The system's adaptability offers a significant improvement over static Bayesian approaches, potentially leading to faster convergence and improved accuracy across diverse probabilistic modeling tasks. The design emphasizes robustness and adaptability, offering a practical solution for tackling complex probabilistic problems where a single, pre-defined algorithm may prove inadequate.

title: Dynamic Programming with Neural Networks for Sequence Alignment
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to sequence alignment leveraging the strengths of dynamic programming and neural networks. The core idea is to replace the computationally intensive, explicit dynamic programming table with a neural network trained to predict alignment scores. This allows for a potentially significant acceleration of the alignment process, particularly for large sequences. We detail the architecture of the neural network, the training methodology, and demonstrate the feasibility of this hybrid approach. The resulting system offers a promising direction for improving the efficiency of sequence alignment algorithms while retaining the accuracy inherent in dynamic programming. The primary contribution lies in the integrated framework, offering a practical alternative to traditional methods. The system's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstration, highlighting the potential for scaling alignment computations.

title: Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing to solve combinatorial optimization problems. The core claim is that quantum annealing algorithms can effectively enhance the efficiency and accuracy of solving such problems. The underlying mechanism involves simulating the quantum annealing process, leveraging the quantum tunneling effect to explore the solution space and identify optimal solutions. This work presents a novel approach by applying quantum annealing to combinatorial optimization, offering a fresh perspective on problem-solving. We explore the theoretical foundations, model the annealing process, and discuss potential challenges and future research directions. The focus is on demonstrating the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach rather than presenting results from experimental implementations.

title: DynamicBUS: restoring temporal dynamics from static ultrasound for improved breast cancer diagnosis
abstract: Abstract The clinical practice of archiving static 2D images from dynamic breast ultrasound (BUS) examinations leads to a critical loss of temporal information, vital for accurate lesion diagnosis. This data limitation constrains the performance of conventional computer-aided diagnosis systems. We challenge this limitation by proposing a novel framework that computationally recovers and leverages these lost temporal dynamics to enhance diagnostic accuracy. Our framework first synthesizes a BUS video from a static key frame image using a purpose-built generative model. For diagnostically plausible synthesis, we introduce a key-frame conditioning strategy that ensures the anatomical fidelity of the lesion is preserved while generating useful dynamic cues. Subsequently, the high-fidelity static image and the synthesized video are fed into our designed IV-Net, a dual-branch fusion network that synergistically integrates pristine spatial details with the recovered temporal context for robust classification. Evaluated on key frame BUS datasets, our integrated framework outperforms methods that rely solely on static images (AUC: 92.63\%).Moreover, a reader study indicates that the generated videos are indistinguishable to experts and lead to higher diagnostic performance. Overall, our method demonstrates the potential of generative AI to restore lost clinical information, paving the way for more accurate and reliable diagnostic systems in BUS diagnosis. The code and generated dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/minnelab/DynamicBUS

title: Hybrid Nature‐Inspired Systems
abstract: Several optimization and complex problems can be easily solved with hybrid frameworks that are inspired by natural systems. Nature-inspired optimization techniques advocates solution-space exploration and finding local optima. The integration of evolutionary schemes with bio-inspired techniques provides appropriate solution for context-aware learning and evolutionary multi-objective optimization. These bio-inspired neural optimization automates the design and hyper parameter tuning of evolved neural networks. The ensemble methods like Hybrid swarm-genetic optimization, Multi-strategy evolutionary algorithm generates optimal results with quicker response. The multi-paradigm approach facilitates operations such as dimensionality reduction, training, deployment, monitoring and decision making. The augmented versions featuring multi-population evolutionary algorithms accelerate scalability and reliability. These evolutionary hybrid systems play a vital role in numerous domains. In healthcare, it helps to identify genetic related disease, drug discovery and personalized managements. In energy sector, it helps to fine-tune the wind turbines in order to achieve economical and efficient power supply. These heterogeneous models optimize the payload patterns in space explorations. The proposed section explores the essential fundamentals, implementations, and real-world applications of different meta-hybrid models.

title: Exploiting Per-Core Leakage: Electromagnetic Side-Channel Monitoring of Multicore Architectures
abstract: Multicore processors are increasingly adopted in embedded systems to meet growing performance demands. However, physical side-channel analysis of multicore architectures remains underexplored, as obtaining usable leakage is inherently challenging. Consequently, side-channel security research on such systems has lagged far behind, leaving a critical security gap. To address this gap, we reveal the electromagnetic leakage mechanisms in multicore architectures and, for the first time, demonstrate per-core leakage exploitation, thereby enabling physical side-channel analysis for these systems. As a practical extension, we present a non-intrusive side-channel monitoring method that achieves per-core granularity. To validate its feasibility and practicality, we implement a prototype on a heterogeneous SoC platform with an RF front-end, and evaluate on a commercial off-the-shelf quad-core embedded system, the Raspberry Pi 4B with ARM Cortex-A72 cores.

title: Rubric-to-Code Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Interactive web application generation requires models to produce usable HTML, CSS, and JavaScript applications from natural language requests. Unlike conventional code generation, application quality depends on multiple user-facing functional requirements, each often tied to localized code regions such as event handlers, state updates, DOM fragments, or CSS selectors. Standard GRPO collapses these structured outcomes into a single sequence-level reward and applies the resulting advantage uniformly to all tokens, weakening credit assignment. We propose Rubric-to-Code Credit Assignment (RCCA), a reinforcement learning framework that converts rubric-level functional feedback into localized optimization signals over generated code. RCCA builds training tasks around explicit functional rubrics, uses a hierarchical reward to separate format, source-code, runtime, and functional failures, and aligns evaluator-generated textual attributions with responsible code spans and generated tokens. title: Analisis Dinamika Sentimen Publik dan Hubungannya dengan Harga BBM Menggunakan Indobert dan Analisis Time Series
abstract: The escalation of geopolitical conflict between Iran, the United States, and Israel in 2026 triggered fluctuations in global oil prices, subsequently driving up domestic fuel prices in Indonesia and provoking various public responses on social media. This study aims to analyze the dynamics of public sentiment toward this issue and examine its temporal relationship with fuel price movements. The research data comprises 3,000 YouTube comments collected during the January–June 2026 period, classified using the IndoBERT model (indobenchmark/indobert-base-p1) fine-tuned with a Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation scheme, Class Weighting, and Focal Loss to address class imbalance. A total of 900 comments were manually labeled as training data, while the remaining 2,069 comments were predicted by the model, resulting in 2,967 fully labeled data points. Weekly sentiment dynamics (n=24) were analyzed using four trend-testing methods (Linear Regression, Mann-Kendall, Spearman Correlation, and Chi-Square/Cramer's V), while the sentiment–fuel price relationship was tested using three approaches (Level Linear Regression, Cross-Correlation Function, and Differenced Regression). Results show the model achieved an average Macro F1-score of 0.7476 (SD=0.0297) with stable performance across folds. Sentiment distribution was dominated by the Negative class (57.1%), followed by Neutral (23.2%) and Positive (19.7%). Trend testing indicated a gradually improving sentiment trend, confirmed by three of four methods, while the relationship analysis found strong lag-3 correlations for three of five fuel types that did not persist under differenced regression, suggesting a possible spurious correlation rather than a confirmed causal relationship.

title: A Systematic Survey of LLM-Based Agentic AI Frameworks for Multi-Agent Coordination and Interoperability
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have spurred the development of agentic artificial intelligence systems that can reason autonomously, plan, use tools, integrate memory, and carry out multi-step tasks. Unlike conventional prompt-response systems, LLM-based agents extend generative models to goal-oriented architectures that can decompose complex objectives, interact with external environments, and coordinate actions in iterative workflows. The survey systematically reviews LLM-based agent frameworks, multi-agent collaboration architectures, internal communication mechanisms, emerging cross-system interoperability protocols, and open research challenges. The review uses a PRISMA-based methodology, including literature from 2020 to March 2026, with particular focus on prominent frameworks such as LangChain, AutoGPT, AutoGen, MetaGPT, CAMEL, ChatDev, and CrewAI. The survey discusses the transition from modular chain-oriented to stateful graph-oriented and autonomous execution models and presents a systematic taxonomy of multi-agent collaboration architectures, including hierarchical, peer-to-peer, and role-based models. It also reviews the main internal communication mechanisms used to facilitate coordination and information sharing between LLM-based agents and distinguishes them from emerging interoperability protocols designed to support interaction across heterogeneous agents, tools, services, and frameworks. The analysis indicates that the promise of LLM-based agents for scalable automation, collaborative reasoning, and complex workflow execution comes with significant challenges in long-horizon reliability, evaluation standardization, communication security, cost-efficient orchestration, governance, and the interpretability of emergent multi-agent behavior. The survey covers architectural evolution, collaboration patterns, communication mechanisms, framework-level characteristics, and open research challenges. This provides a structured foundation for future research on reliable and trustworthy agentic artificial intelligence systems.

title: Optimizing NLP-Text Classification in Knowledge Management Systems: A Literature Review
abstract: Knowledge Management Systems (KMS) are required to organize and assign meaning to huge amounts of organizational knowledge that are largely in the form of unstructured text. Natural Language Processing (NLP), and more immediately methods of text categorization, has been one of the principal enabler technologies to enable KMS to be simpler by helping to automatically categorize documents, enhance searching for information, and assist in decision-making. This paper offers an outline of the evolution of NLP-based text classification methods from initial machine learning methods such as Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machines to current sophisticated deep learning algorithms such as Convolutional Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, and Transformers. We offer real-world industry use cases, issues of scalability, explainability, and ethics and encapsulate research areas of existing gaps. The findings underscore the enormous potential of NLP text classification to assist the effectiveness and efficiency of knowledge management (KM) activities.

title: Neural Network Topology-Guided Embedding Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network embedding learning that leverages the inherent topology of neural networks. Traditional embedding methods often treat neural networks as unstructured collections of nodes, neglecting the crucial spatial and connectivity information. Our proposed methodology explicitly models and optimizes the network topology, recognizing that the physical relationships between neurons – such as connection strength and delay – significantly impact the quality and generalization ability of learned embeddings. We introduce an algorithm that incorporates topological constraints into the embedding process, potentially through regularization terms or graph neural network architectures. This approach demonstrates the potential to improve embedding accuracy and robustness by better capturing complex data relationships. The core claim is that utilizing topological information during embedding significantly enhances embedding quality and generalization. The core mechanism involves developing an algorithm that simultaneously considers input/output relationships and explicitly models and optimizes the network topology.

title: 基于量子纠错码的分布式数据库管理
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed database management leveraging quantum error correction codes (QECCs). Traditional distributed databases face significant challenges in data reliability and fault tolerance, particularly with increasing data volumes and complex query processing. This research explores the application of QECCs to encode and decode database data, thereby enhancing data integrity during transmission and storage. The core claim is that the utilization of QECCs can dramatically improve the robustness and reliability of distributed database systems. This work details the theoretical framework, focusing on the encoding and decoding processes using specific QECC families. The key mechanism involves the redundancy introduced by QECCs, allowing for the detection and correction of errors without requiring complete data reconstruction. This approach offers a potential solution to the inherent limitations of classical distributed databases. Further investigation into practical implementation considerations and performance analysis is warranted.

title: Quantum Error Correction Based Topological Protected Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for quantum neural networks (QNNs) that leverages the benefits of topological protection and quantum error correction (QEC). The core idea is to construct a QNN based on a network of non-Abelian anyons, exploiting their inherent robustness against local perturbations. We introduce a framework where topological protection significantly reduces the impact of noise on the network, while LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) codes are employed to actively correct errors in the quantum information. The resulting system demonstrates a high tolerance to noise, a critical requirement for scalable QNN implementations. This approach represents a significant advancement in QNN design, merging the strengths of topological quantum computing and established QEC techniques. The theoretical framework outlines the key components and provides a pathway toward realizing fault-tolerant QNNs. The proposed architecture offers a promising route toward building practical and reliable quantum computing systems.

title: Distributed Simulation of Physical Systems using Quantum Simulation Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum simulation algorithms to achieve distributed simulation of complex physical systems. The core concept involves breaking down computationally intensive simulations—such as fluid dynamics or molecular interactions—into smaller, manageable subproblems solvable on multiple quantum processors. These subproblem solutions are then integrated through quantum communication protocols. The research investigates the theoretical framework for such an approach, focusing on algorithm design, communication strategies, and the challenges associated with achieving efficient distributed simulation. This work demonstrates a practical application of quantum computing for large-scale simulation tasks, offering a novel methodology for tackling problems currently intractable for classical computers. We detail the key considerations for designing a robust and scalable distributed simulation system, including error mitigation techniques and the impact of quantum communication fidelity on overall simulation accuracy.

title: Formal Modeling of Quantum Circuits with Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuits, fundamental to quantum computation, represent quantum states through a sequence of unitary transformations. The exponential growth in the Hilbert space dimension with increasing circuit size presents a significant challenge to simulation and analysis. This work introduces a novel tensor network approach to formally model and manipulate quantum circuits, specifically designed to mitigate this exponential scaling issue. The core idea is to represent the circuit's state vector as a tensor network, leveraging techniques for efficient compression and expansion. We explore the application of variational tensor networks (VTNs) to approximate the dynamics of quantum circuits, offering a pathway towards more scalable simulations. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, focusing on key aspects of tensor network construction and manipulation tailored to quantum circuit representations. This approach aims to provide a more scalable representation compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Key Distribution for Secure Communication Protocols
abstract: This paper proposes a novel secure communication protocol based on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The core claim is to design a protocol capable of completely secure key transmission, resisting eavesdropping and manipulation, thereby guaranteeing communication security. The protocol leverages quantum entanglement to facilitate quantum key transmission and employs cryptographic algorithms for key encryption and decryption. Traditional secure communication protocols relying on classical key exchange are vulnerable to attacks. QKD offers a significantly higher level of security. This document details the protocol's architecture, mathematical formulation of the key exchange process, and the security analysis underpinning its design. The focus is on demonstrating a robust system against known classical and quantum attacks, providing a foundation for future secure communication networks. The system is designed for a two-party communication scenario, aiming for maximal security with reasonable complexity.

title: Imagining Trajectories for Anomaly Detection in Reinforcement Learning from Images
abstract: Abstract Detecting anomalous inputs is a critical prerequisite for the safe deployment of reinforcement learning (RL) agents in real-world environments. Although anomaly detection (AD) has been extensively studied in other domains, its application to reinforcement learning remains challenging due to high-dimensional sensory observations and complex temporal dependencies. Existing approaches in this setting are limited and often rely on access to internal representations of trained agents, creating an undesirable coupling between policy and safety mechanisms. In this work, we propose ITRM, a novel approach to anomaly detection in visual reinforcement learning that is fully agent-agnostic and does not require access to policy internals. Our method is based on the observation that deviations from nominal environment dynamics can be identified through discrepancies in the latent representations of a learned world model. Specifically, we leverage predictive components of a recurrent state-space model to generate deterministic latent embeddings that serve as normative references for anomaly detection. Anomalies are detected by comparing predicted latent features against a reference set of nominal embeddings using a similarity-based criterion. Operating in the world model’s latent space allows the detector to capture semantically meaningful deviations. Extensive empirical evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves strong detection performance. On the Anomaly-Gym benchmark, our method outperforms existing baselines, achieving an average AUROC of 0.853 and an FPR95 of 0.279.

title: Rényi Entanglement of Purification Is Non-additive
abstract: Entanglement of purification is a fundamental measure of total correlations whose additivity remains unresolved. We study its additivity for classical states on two qubits at different Rényi orders. For every $α\in[0,1)$, we prove nonadditivity within this family, witnessed by two copies of a single state. We first solve the one-copy optimization exactly for the entire family at every Rényi order. We then restrict the two-copy optimization to a natural finite set of purifications and exhibit one whose entropy is strictly below the product value. In contrast, for $α\in[2,\infty]$ we prove additivity under tensor products within this family. The interval $α\in[1,2)$, including the von Neumann case $α=1$, remains open, and we conjecture additivity there throughout the same family.

title: Kerr nonlinearity and three-wave mixing in superconducting resonators hosting Al-InAs weak links
abstract: Nonlinear microwave resonators are a versatile tool in quantum information processing, enabling parametric amplification, continuous variable quantum computing, and engineered mode interactions. Many of these applications especially benefit from cubic nonlinearities enabling three-wave mixing; at the same time, they are limited by quartic nonlinearities giving rise to undesired Kerr effects. A recurrent challenge is therefore to engineer resonators with a finite cubic nonlinearity while suppressing quartic terms. Here, we investigate a superconducting resonator hosting two weak links fabricated from an aluminum-capped indium arsenide nanowire. We characterize the Kerr nonlinearity as a function of magnetic flux and gate bias, showing that it can be tuned to zero with either control parameter. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate three-wave mixing in a semiconductor-superconductor hybrid device, establishing nonzero cubic nonlinearity. An effective model based on Andreev bound states qualitatively captures the observed trends. Our results validate semiconductor-superconductor hybrid devices as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear superconducting circuits, with applications in parametric amplification, quantum control of bosonic modes, and engineering interactions between microwave modes.

title: OpenStamp: A Watermark for Open-Source Language Models
abstract: With the growing prevalence of large language model (LLM) generated content, watermarking is considered a promising approach for attributing text to LLMs and distinguishing it from human-written content. A prominent class of techniques embeds subtle but detectable signals in generated text by modifying token sampling probabilities. However, such methods are unsuitable for open-source models, where users have white-box access and can easily disable watermarking during inference. In this work, we introduce OpenStamp, a watermarking technique that encodes the watermarking logic directly into the model weights by modifying only the final projection, or unembedding, layer. Through experiments across two models, we show that OpenStamp achieves superior detection performance, with minimal degradation in model capabilities compared to prior methods. The implanted watermark is explicitly designed, and empirically confirmed, to be more robust to paraphrasing attacks and harder to scrub off through post-hoc fine-tuning than prior open-source watermarks. To enable developers to watermark their models, we release our code alongside watermarked versions of 4 popular open-source models.

title: Quantum Computation Security Based on Quantum Demagnetization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to achieving high-security distributed computing by leveraging the principles of quantum demagnetization. Current distributed computing security strategies predominantly rely on cryptographic techniques, which are increasingly vulnerable to attacks from quantum computers. This research introduces a system architecture that decomposes computational tasks into multiple quantum sub-programs and employs quantum demagnetization to guarantee the independence and security of these sub-programs, thus mitigating the risks of malicious attacks and data breaches. The core claim is the utilization of quantum demagnetization to construct a highly secure distributed computing architecture. The key mechanism involves partitioning computational tasks into independent quantum subprograms, ensuring their security through quantum demagnetization, thereby preventing unauthorized access and data leakage. This approach represents a fundamentally new security paradigm, offering resilience against quantum threats that traditional cryptographic methods cannot effectively address. The system's architecture is designed for scalability and adaptability, offering a robust solution for sensitive distributed computing applications. Mathematical formulations and key concepts are presented to demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of the proposed system.

This research introduces a system architecture that decomposes computational tasks into multiple quantum sub-programs and employs quantum demagnetization to guarantee the independence and security of these sub-programs, thus mitigating the risks of malicious attacks and data breaches. The core claim is the utilization of quantum demagnetization to construct a highly secure distributed computing architecture. The key mechanism involves partitioning computational tasks into independent quantum subprograms, ensuring their security through quantum demagnetization, thereby preventing unauthorized access and data leakage. This approach represents a fundamentally new security paradigm, offering resilience against quantum threats that traditional cryptographic methods cannot effectively address. The system's architecture is designed for scalability and adaptability, offering a robust solution for sensitive distributed computing applications. Mathematical formulations and key concepts are presented to demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of the proposed system.
